title: Hall and Yard
text:
1. The facility comprises a single warehouse hall with an enclosed floor of 6,000 m2 and an external yard serving the dock apron and manoeuvring area.

2. High-bay pallet racking occupies the bulk storage area and provides 2,400 pallet positions for standard pallets.

3. The building envelope provides 8 dock doors along one elevation for inbound receiving and outbound dispatch.

All operational activity takes place within the hall, the dock approaches and the yard. No storage or staging occurs outside the marked internal zones without specific authorisation.

4. Zone F contains support functions ancillary to storage and picking, including the hazmat cage, which covers 60 m2 inside Zone F.

5. The hall layout separates bulk storage, picking, receiving, dispatch and temperature-controlled areas into defined floor zones. Each zone retains its designated purpose during both operational shifts.

6. Shift 1 runs 06:00-14:00, Monday to Friday, and holds responsibility for the site from handover at 06:00 until transfer to the second shift.

7. Shift 2 runs 14:00-22:00, Monday to Friday, and maintains continuity of operations, safety checks and handover discipline through to site closure at 22:00.

The two-shift pattern provides continuous weekday cover within the same physical footprint. Staffing levels and MHE deployment vary by shift, but floor area, pallet positions and dock availability remain constant.

8. Capacity planning for inbound, storage and outbound activity must use the hall figure of 6,000 m2, the racking provision of 2,400 pallet positions and the availability of 8 dock doors as fixed constraints.

9. Housekeeping and aisle clearance standards apply across the entire 6,000 m2 floor regardless of shift. Keep main routes, dock approaches and the 60 m2 hazmat cage perimeter free of obstruction at all times.

title: Floor Zones A–F
text:
1. Zone A is the receiving zone: inbound docks 1-4, unloading and goods inspection. Inbound Operators work in Zone A to unload, count and inspect deliveries before booking. Vehicles assigned to Zone A use docks 1-4 only. No outbound staging takes place in Zone A.

2. Zone B is the bulk storage zone: high-bay pallet racking. Put-away from Zone A moves directly to Zone B rack locations. Stock in Zone B supplies replenishment to Zone C. Access in Zone B follows rack aisle controls.

3. Zone C is the picking zone: ground-level pick faces and flow racks. Pickers operate in Zone C against scanner tasks to fulfil customer orders. Replenishment keeps Zone C pick faces filled from Zone B. Packing preparation also starts from picks completed in Zone C.

4. Zone D is the dispatch zone: outbound staging in front of docks 5-8. Outbound loads are staged, wrapped and released in Zone D. Dispatchers assign docks 5-8 for loading in Zone D. Carriers collect only from Zone D doors.

5. Zone E is the cold zone: chilled storage held at +2 to +6 °C. Product requiring temperature control is stored only in Zone E. Doors to Zone E remain closed except for put-away and picking moves. Monitoring keeps Zone E within its +2 to +6 °C range.

6. Zone F holds the value-added services area. The quarantine area is in Zone F for holds pending release. Returns are inspected in Zone F before any disposition. The hazmat cage is inside Zone F for segregated storage. The hazmat cage inside Zone F covers 60 m2.

Circulation between zones uses the marked aisle network.

7. Main transport aisles are 4.0 m wide. These aisles link Zone A through Zone B and Zone C to Zone D, with branches to Zone E and Zone F. Counterbalance forklifts and reach trucks use main transport aisles for longer moves. Keep main transport aisles clear of staging at all times.

8. Rack storage aisles are 3.0 m wide. Rack storage aisles are located inside Zone B between high-bay runs. Only materials handling equipment and authorised persons enter rack storage aisles when handling pallets.

9. Segregated pedestrian walkways are 1.2 m wide. Walkways provide protected routes through and around Zone A, Zone B, Zone C, Zone D, Zone E and Zone F. Do not block segregated pedestrian walkways with pallets, cages or waste. Cross only at marked crossing points.

title: Docks and Yard Access
text:
1. The building provides 8 dock doors on the dock face. Keep the yard approach clear and use only the door assigned to your vehicle.

2. Dock doors 1-4 serve inbound receiving. Position inbound trailers at these doors only. Follow PR-01 Inbound receiving for arrival, document check and unloading.

3. Dock doors 5-8 serve outbound dispatch. There are 4 outbound dock doors. Position outbound trailers at these doors only. Follow PR-06 Outbound dispatch for staging, final checks and load release.

4. Each of the 8 dock doors has a dock leveller. Deploy the leveller only after the vehicle is chocked and the dock door is fully open. Retract the leveller before the vehicle departs and report any defect immediately.

5. The dispatcher assigns dock doors and time slots to carriers. Dispatchers book transport, assign dock doors and release outbound loads. Do not approach a door or move to the waiting area without dispatcher confirmation.

6. For inbound operations, report to the inbound waiting area at your booked time slot. Present documents at Zone A for the document check in accordance with PR-01 Inbound receiving. Wait for the dispatcher to call you forward to doors 1-4.

7. For outbound operations, stage loads in Zone D in front of docks 5-8. Each outbound door handles 4 trailer loads per shift. Outbound capacity is at most 448 full-weight pallets per shift. Adding trailer capacity beyond the 448 full-weight pallet per shift limit requires warehouse manager agreement. Do not load past the assigned door and do not release a load without dispatcher release under PR-06 Outbound dispatch.

8. Separate pedestrians and trucks at the doors. Use the marked pedestrian doors and segregated walkways. Do not walk across dock leveller approaches when a leveller is deployed or a forklift is in motion.

9. Observe yard and dock speed limits at all times:

10. Do not exceed 12 km/h in the outdoor yard.

11. Do not exceed 8 km/h inside the building.

12. Do not exceed 5 km/h on dock ramps and leveller approaches. Slow before the ramp, maintain control on the leveller and do not overtake on the approach.

13. Main transport aisles feeding the docks are 4.0 m wide. Keep these aisles clear of pallets, waste and parked MHE to maintain access for counterbalance trucks and emergency egress.

title: Roles on Site
text:
1. Warehouse Manager
The warehouse manager is accountable for the whole site: operations, safety and final sign-offs. This role holds overall responsibility for operational performance, compliance and safe working across all zones.
Direct all departments, approve key operational decisions and ensure procedures are followed consistently.

2. Shift Supervisor
The shift supervisor runs one shift: floor staff and incident response. During the assigned shift, this role directs activity on the floor, allocates tasks and responds first to operational incidents.
Maintain shift discipline, communicate priorities and escalate issues requiring higher approval.

3. Forklift Operator
Forklift operators operate forklifts, reach trucks and pallet jacks. Operators handle internal transport, place and retrieve pallets and support loading and unloading tasks as directed.
Work only with authorised equipment, follow assigned scanner or supervisor instructions and report defects immediately.

4. Picker
Pickers pick customer orders in Zone C against scanner tasks. All picking activity follows system-directed tasks in the picking zone.
Complete picks accurately, handle stock with care and confirm each transaction on the handheld device.

5. Inbound Operator
Inbound operators unload, count and inspect inbound goods in Zone A. Work centres on the receiving zone at inbound docks, covering physical unloading and initial verification.
Check deliveries against documentation, record quantities and identify damage or discrepancies for further action.

6. Stock Controller
Stock controllers own inventory accuracy: cycle counts, recounts and adjustments. This function governs stock integrity across the warehouse.
Plan and execute counting activities, investigate variances and prepare adjustments for approval.

7. Returns Staff
Returns staff inspect returns in Zone F and propose restock, rework or scrap. All returns activity is centred in Zone F, where items are assessed after receipt.
Evaluate condition, document findings and submit a disposition recommendation for approval.

8. Maintenance Technician
The maintenance technician maintains MHE, racking and dock equipment and logs all repairs. Responsibility covers mechanical handling equipment, storage racking and dock infrastructure.
Carry out preventive maintenance, attend breakdowns promptly and maintain a complete record of repairs undertaken.

9. Dispatcher
Dispatchers book transport, assign dock doors and release outbound loads. This role controls the outbound flow from staging to departure.
Coordinate carriers, allocate dock doors and time slots and authorise the release of completed loads for transport.

title: Approvals and Accountability
text:
1. The warehouse manager is accountable for the whole site: operations, safety and final sign-offs. No other role carries this overall accountability.

2. The shift supervisor runs one shift: floor staff and incident response. The shift supervisor exercises approval authority only within that shift and escalates all matters beyond the defined thresholds to the warehouse manager.

3. Under PR-08 Stocktaking and cycle counts, only the warehouse manager may sign off stocktake results. No stocktake is closed, posted or communicated to the client until that sign-off is obtained. Stock controllers own inventory accuracy through cycle counts, recounts and adjustments, but they do not hold sign-off authority.

4. Under PR-09 Damaged-goods handling, damaged-goods write-offs above 750 EUR need warehouse manager approval. The threshold is applied as follows:
  a) The shift supervisor approves damaged-goods write-offs up to 750 EUR.
  b) The warehouse manager approves damaged-goods write-offs above 750 EUR.
  c) For damaged-goods write-offs above 750 EUR the shift supervisor must endorse the request and forward it to the warehouse manager for final decision.
Submit the damage report, value calculation and photographs to the relevant approver before scrapping, disposal or system write-off. Do not split a single damage event to remain below the threshold.

5. Under PR-07 Returns handling, the shift supervisor approves the final disposition of inspected returns. Returns staff inspect returns in Zone F and propose restock, rework or scrap, but the disposition takes effect only after shift supervisor approval. Do not move inspected returns back to stock until approval is recorded.

6. Only the warehouse manager may approve overtime. Request overtime in advance with reason, hours and staff required. Do not work or record overtime hours without written approval from the warehouse manager.

7. The shift supervisor reviews every incident report. Submit all injuries, near misses, equipment damage and procedural deviations to the shift supervisor on duty. Carry out corrective actions assigned from that review and close the report only when the shift supervisor confirms completion.

8. Only the warehouse manager may authorise new forklift operators. No operator may drive counterbalance forklifts, reach trucks or other MHE until the warehouse manager has issued authorisation. Maintain the authorisation register centrally and withdraw authorisation where training or medical requirements lapse.

9. Accountability for communication at shift change rests with the outgoing and incoming shift supervisors under PR-15 End-of-shift handover. Complete the handover record, note open approvals, pending write-offs and outstanding incident reviews, and obtain acknowledgement from the incoming shift supervisor.

title: Shift Leadership and Dock Control
text:
1. The shift supervisor runs one shift: floor staff and incident response. The role provides continuous floor leadership across both operating windows.

2. Shift coverage is as follows:
 a. Shift 1 runs 06:00-14:00, Monday to Friday.
 b. Shift 2 runs 14:00-22:00, Monday to Friday.
 Each shift has a designated shift supervisor accountable for personnel deployment, task allocation and first response to operational and safety incidents during that shift.

3. The shift supervisor holds the following decision authorities on the floor:
 a. Approve damaged-goods write-offs up to 750 EUR.
 b. Approve the final disposition of inspected returns following inspection in Zone F.
 c. Review every incident report raised on shift.
 For damaged-goods write-offs above 750 EUR the shift supervisor endorses the request and forwards it to the warehouse manager for final decision. Escalations above these thresholds pass to the warehouse manager under Chapter 2.2.

4. Dispatchers book transport, assign dock doors and release outbound loads. The function controls all vehicle movements to and from the building.

5. The dispatcher assigns dock doors and time slots to carriers. Allocation follows the fixed door designation:
 a. Dock doors 1-4 serve inbound receiving.
 b. Dock doors 5-8 serve outbound dispatch.
 No carrier may occupy a door without a scheduled assignment from the dispatcher.

6. Coordination between the shift supervisor and the dispatcher is mandatory at shift start, mid-shift and before end-of-shift handover:
 a. The dispatcher confirms the inbound and outbound door plan for doors 1-4 and 5-8.
 b. The shift supervisor confirms staffing for unloading in Zone A, replenishment and picking in Zones B and C, and staging in Zone D.
 c. Both roles align on priorities for delayed carriers, labour constraints and incident impacts.

7. During live operations, the shift supervisor retains authority for floor safety and manning, while the dispatcher retains authority for the door schedule. If a safety incident requires a door to be closed or a load to be held, the shift supervisor directs the immediate action and the dispatcher re-books the affected time slot.

8. All releases of outbound loads from Zone D remain with the dispatcher. Forklift operators and pickers must not release or dispatch a load without dispatcher authorisation, even when staging is complete.

title: Working Hours
text:
1. The site operates on two weekday shifts. Plan all receiving, storage, picking and dispatch activity within these windows and staff each function to cover its full span.
2. Shift 1 runs 06:00-14:00, Monday to Friday. All Zone A receiving, Zone B and Zone C replenishment, and early outbound preparation fall within this shift.
3. Shift 2 runs 14:00-22:00, Monday to Friday. Late picking, packing, loading at docks and final releases are completed before close of this shift.
4. There is no routine weekend working. Any activity outside 06:00-14:00 and 14:00-22:00, Monday to Friday, counts as overtime and requires separate approval.
5. The warehouse manager is accountable for the whole site: operations, safety and final sign-offs. The warehouse manager sets shift rosters, confirms cover for both shifts, and is the point of accountability for hours worked and compliance with working-time limits.
6. The shift supervisor runs one shift: floor staff and incident response. Each shift has a designated shift supervisor present on the floor for the entire 06:00-14:00 or 14:00-22:00 period, responsible for task allocation, safety compliance and first response to incidents during that shift.
7. Duties by role for working hours are:
  1) Warehouse manager — publish weekly roster; confirm minimum cover for Zone A to Zone F tasks; authorise overtime; sign off any change to shift start or finish times.
  2) Shift supervisor — run the assigned shift; brief staff at start-of-shift; monitor attendance; escalate short-cover or disruption to the warehouse manager; close the shift in line with PR-15 End-of-shift handover.
  3) All other roles — attend the rostered shift; report late arrival or absence to the shift supervisor immediately; remain on task until formally handed over or released.
8. Overtime rule:
  1) Request overtime in advance through the shift supervisor, stating reason, hours and staff required.
  2) Only the warehouse manager may approve overtime. No overtime is worked on verbal approval from any other role.
  3) Record approved overtime by date, shift, staff names and hours; retain the record for payroll and audit.
  4) Do not use overtime to bypass roster controls. Adjust rosters first within 06:00-14:00 and 14:00-22:00, Monday to Friday, before seeking overtime.
9. At the end of each shift, complete PR-15 End-of-shift handover before staff leave the floor. Hand over unfinished receiving, put-away, picking and dispatch tasks, equipment status and any incidents to the incoming shift supervisor or, for Shift 2, to the warehouse manager’s night log. Do not leave tasks unassigned at shift end.
10. Coordinate all cross-shift work through the two shift supervisors and the warehouse manager. Keep handover notes short, task-specific and tied to zones and procedure numbers.

title: End-of-Shift Handover
text:
1. Apply Procedure PR-15 End-of-shift handover at every change of supervisor.

The outgoing shift supervisor hands over to the incoming shift supervisor face-to-face on the warehouse floor. Do not hand over by phone, message or written note alone.

2. Accountability for the handover.

The shift supervisor runs one shift: floor staff and incident response. The outgoing supervisor remains accountable until the incoming supervisor confirms acceptance of the handover. Record both names and the handover time in the shift log.

3. Review status of people, equipment and work.

Brief the following in order and note exceptions:

a) Staffing and incidents. Report headcount present, absences, injuries and near misses. The shift supervisor reviews every incident report. Hand over any open incident reports, witness details and immediate actions taken.

b) Cycle counts. Cycle counts run every working day on a rotating zone schedule. State which zone was counted, results, recounts required and stock adjustments awaiting approval.

c) MHE availability. Every forklift gets a documented pre-use check each day. Report trucks out of service, battery status, defects logged and checks still due for the next shift. Hand over keys and defect sheets.

d) Cold zone. Cold-zone temperature is manually verified each shift. Report the last manual verification for Zone E, any excursion, corrective action and whether product is on hold.

4. Hand over active operational controls.

Confirm dock door assignments, outbound loads in progress, replenishment tasks outstanding and any quarantine or hazmat movements in Zone F. Identify orders at risk and agree priorities for the next shift.

5. Communicate safety and site conditions.

Report housekeeping issues, spills, rack damage, pedestrian restrictions and maintenance work in progress. Confirm that segregated walkways and aisles are clear.

6. Confirm emergency status.

If an evacuation has occurred, confirm that Procedure PR-14 Emergency evacuation was followed and that roll call at the assembly point happens before anyone re-enters the building. Do not authorise re-entry until roll call is complete and the all-clear is given. Hand over the evacuation log, missing-person checks and any building damage.

7. Close the handover.

The incoming shift supervisor repeats back critical items: open incidents, equipment out of service, cold-zone status and priority orders. Resolve discrepancies immediately. Both supervisors sign the handover record. The incoming supervisor then briefs floor staff and assumes control of floor staff and incident response for the new shift.

title: Arrival and Door Assignment
text:
1. Apply PR-01 Inbound receiving to every inbound arrival from yard entry to door assignment.
2. The building has 8 dock doors. Dock doors 1-4 serve inbound receiving.
3. Zone A is the receiving zone: inbound docks 1-4, unloading and goods inspection. Hold vehicles and goods in Zone A until the receiving steps are complete.
4. The dispatcher assigns dock doors and time slots to carriers. Contact the dispatcher on arrival and await a door allocation. Do not allocate doors from the floor.
5. The dispatcher books transport, assigns dock doors and releases outbound loads. Keep inbound assignments and outbound releases under dispatcher control to avoid door conflicts.
6. Complete the document check BEFORE unloading. Verify the delivery note, purchase order and carrier identity against the booked slot. Inbound operators unload, count and inspect inbound goods in Zone A only after the check passes.
7. Reject or quarantine mismatched paperwork before breaking any seal. Record discrepancies and notify the dispatcher before proceeding.
8. Enforce PPE at the dock and in the yard. High-visibility vests are mandatory for everyone on the warehouse floor. Safety footwear class S3 is mandatory on the warehouse floor.
9. Control forklift movement during arrival and docking. Forklifts must not exceed 8 km/h inside the building. Forklifts must not exceed 12 km/h in the outdoor yard.
10. Forklifts must slow to 5 km/h in marked pedestrian zones and crossings. Give way to pedestrians at all marked crossings on approach to Zone A.
11. Forklifts must not exceed 5 km/h on dock ramps and leveller approaches. Approach dock doors 1-4 squarely and stop to check leveller status before entering the trailer.
12. Inbound operators take ownership of the door once assigned. Unload, count and inspect inbound goods in Zone A, keep the door area clear, and report completion to the dispatcher for system booking.

title: Unloading, Count and Inspection
text:
1. Apply PR-01 Inbound receiving in Zone A for all inbound receipts. Zone A is the receiving zone: inbound docks 1-4, unloading and goods inspection.

2. Wear mandatory personal protective equipment on the warehouse floor. High-visibility vests are mandatory for everyone on the warehouse floor. Safety footwear class S3 is mandatory on the warehouse floor.

3. Complete the document check before unloading. At receiving, the document check happens before unloading.

4. Assign the task only to inbound operators. Inbound operators unload, count and inspect inbound goods in Zone A.

5. Position the vehicle at the assigned inbound dock and apply brakes and wheel chocks. Verify the dock leveller is secured before entering the trailer.

6. Unload pallets to the Zone A inspection lane by load reference. Keep inbound pallets clear of outbound staging and main aisles.

7. Count every pallet, carton and unit against the delivery note and purchase order. Record shortages, overages and visible damage immediately in the WMS using a handheld WMS scanner.

8. Draw handheld WMS scanners from the shared pool. Pickers and inbound staff share 20 handheld WMS scanners. Return each scanner to its charging dock after use and report faults to the shift supervisor.

9. Inspect all inbound goods before system booking. Inbound goods are inspected before they are booked into the system.

10. Check each pallet for:
  a) correct product code, batch and quantity;
  b) intact packaging, seals and labelling;
  c) signs of damage, leakage, contamination or temperature abuse;
  d) pallet integrity and stability.

11. Verify pallet weight at inspection. A pallet, including its load, may weigh at most 900 kg. Reject or reconfigure overweight pallets and record the action on the goods receipt.

12. Segregate non-conforming goods identified during inspection:
  a) move damaged or suspect stock to the quarantine area in Zone F;
  b) attach a hold label with reason, quantity, date and operator initials;
  c) notify the shift supervisor for disposition under PR-09 Damaged-goods handling.

13. Photograph damage where required and file images against the receipt number. Do not book damaged stock into available inventory.

14. Obtain inbound operator sign-off on the count and inspection record. Pass only inspected and accepted quantities forward for system booking and release to put-away.

15. Leave Zone A clear, sweep debris and remove banding and shrink wrap to designated waste containers. Report any spill, unsafe packaging or vehicle defect to the shift supervisor before releasing the dock.

title: System Booking and Release to Put-Away
text:
1. Apply PR-01 Inbound receiving to close the receiving task in Zone A and apply PR-02 Put-away to storage to release pallets to Zone B, Zone E or Zone F. No pallet leaves Zone A for put-away until both procedures are satisfied in order.

2. Inbound operators unload, count and inspect inbound goods in Zone A. Complete the count and inspection fully and resolve discrepancies on the inbound paperwork before creating any system booking. Do not book damaged, short or unidentified stock as available.

3. Observe the booking sequence:
   a. Inspection, then system booking. Inbound goods are inspected BEFORE they are booked into the system under PR-01.
   b. System booking, then put-away. Goods are booked into the system BEFORE put-away to storage under PR-02.
   Follow this order for every pallet without exception.

4. Book receipts on the WMS using the handheld scanners. Pickers and inbound staff share 20 handheld WMS scanners; return the device to its charge bay after booking and report any scanning failure to the shift supervisor immediately. Enter the exact quantity verified at inspection, the pallet ID, and the storage requirement indicated on the purchase order or product master.

5. Assign the put-away destination at booking:
   a. Zone B is the bulk storage zone: high-bay pallet racking. Use for general ambient pallets.
   b. Zone E is the cold zone: chilled storage held at +2 to +6 °C. Use only for temperature-controlled product and confirm the cold-chain status is intact.
   c. Zone F holds the value-added services area. Use for labelling, kitting or other value-added work instructed on the receipt.
   Direct the forklift operator to the assigned zone on the WMS put-away task. Do not stage pallets for Zone B, Zone E or Zone F outside their designated lanes.

6. Route exceptions to quarantine or hazmat holding:
   a. Move any pallet failing inspection, requiring quality review, or awaiting approval to the quarantine area in Zone F. Hold it on system status quarantine.
   b. Move packaged hazardous material requiring segregation to the hazmat cage inside Zone F. Hold it on system status hazmat hold.
   Do not book quarantine or hazmat pallets as available for sale and do not put them away to Zone B or Zone E.

7. Release the put-away task only when the WMS shows status booked and the destination zone is confirmed. Attach the signed inbound receipt to the booking record in PR-01, then generate the PR-02 put-away task. Hand over the pallets with scanner confirmation at the Zone A boundary.

title: Bulk Storage in Zone B
text:
1. Zone B is the bulk storage zone: high-bay pallet racking.

Zone B holds the site's primary pallet inventory. The high-bay racking provides 2,400 pallet positions for standard pallets. All put-away to this zone follows PR-02 Put-away to storage.

2. Complete system booking before any physical put-away.

Do not move goods to Zone B until the WMS booking is confirmed. Goods are booked into the system BEFORE put-away to storage. Use the designated main transport aisles to transfer booked pallets from receiving into Zone B.

3. Observe bay load and pallet weight limits in every location.

Check the bay label before placing stock. Each rack bay may carry at most 2,700 kg. A pallet, including its load, may weigh at most 900 kg. Calculate the total bay load before adding a pallet and leave the bay empty if the limit would be exceeded.

4. Use the correct truck for the task and aisle.

Main transport aisles are 4.0 m wide. Rack storage aisles are 3.0 m wide. Operate counterbalance forklifts in the main aisles and approach bays squarely. The fleet has 9 electric counterbalance forklifts rated at 3.0 t for transport and low-level placement. The fleet has 5 reach trucks rated at 2.0 t for the high bays. Select the reach truck for any placement above lower levels and verify capacity against pallet weight before lifting.

5. Apply block-stacking limits where free stacking is authorised.

Where pallets are approved for free block-stacking outside racking, observe both limits together. Free block-stacked pallets must not exceed 4.0 m in height. Free block-stacked pallets must not exceed 3 pallets high. Stop stacking when either limit is reached and report any leaning or damaged stack to the shift supervisor immediately.

6. Maintain access and inspection readiness.

Keep main aisles and rack storage aisles clear of staging, waste or trailing equipment. Position pallets fully within beams with no overhang into the aisle envelope. Racking gets a documented safety inspection every month. Do not use any bay marked as damaged or under inspection and log defects for the maintenance technician without delay.

title: Cold Zone E
text:
1. Zone E is the cold zone: chilled storage held at +2 to +6 °C. Hold only chilled product in Zone E and keep doors closed except for put-away and picking moves.

2. Maintain the cold zone at or above +2 °C at all times. Check the automated monitoring display on entry and do not store product if the reading is below the minimum.

3. Maintain the cold zone at or below +6 °C at all times. Treat any reading above the maximum as an incident under PR-12 Cold-chain handling and notify the shift supervisor immediately.

4. Manually verify cold-zone temperature each shift. Record the manual reading, time and initials on the Zone E temperature log and countersign any corrective action.

5. Inbound operators unload, count and inspect inbound goods in Zone A. Keep chilled goods staged in Zone A only for the time needed to complete inspection.

6. Apply PR-12 Cold-chain handling to every chilled inbound. Prioritise chilled pallets for inspection and move them to Zone E without delay after release.

7. Complete system booking before put-away to storage. Follow PR-02 Put-away to storage for the booking sequence: goods are booked into the system BEFORE put-away to storage.

8. Do not put away unbooked pallets to Zone E. Confirm the storage location in the WMS, then transport the pallet directly to the assigned cold location.

9. Observe the pallet limit for all Zone E put-away. A pallet, including its load, may weigh at most 900 kg; reject or split any pallet exceeding this weight before put-away.

10. Store pallets to preserve airflow and temperature stability. Keep pallets off door thresholds, maintain circulation gaps and return monitoring probes to position after each move.

11. Report any temperature alarm, door fault or product exposure to the shift supervisor for review under PR-12 Cold-chain handling. Quarantine affected stock and do not pick or dispatch until cleared.

title: Quarantine and Hazmat Cage in Zone F
text:
1. Zone F holds the value-added services area. Keep its three functions physically separate and clearly signed: the quarantine area, the returns inspection area and the hazmat cage.

2. The quarantine area is in Zone F. Use it only for goods held under PR-09 Damaged-goods handling and for any stock awaiting a quality or stock-controller decision. Do not put away quarantined pallets to Zone B, Zone C or Zone E. Do not release quarantined stock until the hold is lifted in the system.

3. Inspect all returns in Zone F. Returns staff inspect returns in Zone F and propose restock, rework or scrap for each item. Place the inspected goods in the quarantine area when they cannot be returned directly to stock. Obtain the required approval before any restock, rework or scrap decision.

4. Handle damaged goods under PR-09 Damaged-goods handling. Move damaged pallets to the quarantine area in Zone F immediately. Record the damage, quantity and location in the WMS. Do not dispose, rework or restock until the authorised approver has signed the disposition.

5. The hazmat cage is inside Zone F. The hazmat cage inside Zone F covers 60 m2 and is locked at all times except during authorised put-away or picking. Permit entry only to trained operators listed on the hazmat authorisation roster. Apply PR-13 Hazmat handling and spill response for every movement, storage check and spill.

6. Observe the stock limit for the hazmat cage at all times:
   a) No more than 3,000 kg of hazmat may be stored in the hazmat cage at one time.
   b) A pallet, including its load, may weigh at most 900 kg.
   c) The hazmat cage therefore holds at most 3 full-weight pallets. Calculate the remaining capacity before each put-away and do not exceed the 3,000 kg limit, even if floor space remains.

7. Complete system booking before any put-away to the cage. Goods are booked into the system BEFORE put-away to storage under PR-02 Put-away to storage. Then execute PR-02 Put-away to storage:
   a) Verify the booking, hazard class and weight on the handheld.
   b) Transport the pallet to Zone F on the designated hazmat route.
   c) Place the pallet only in the assigned cage location and confirm the put-away by scan.

8. Maintain segregation and housekeeping in Zone F:
   a) Never store hazmat outside the cage, even temporarily.
   b) Never store non-hazmat goods inside the cage.
   c) Keep spill kits, fire extinguishers and safety data sheets at the cage entrance as defined in PR-13 Hazmat handling and spill response.
   d) Keep the quarantine area clear of outbound staging. Outbound staging uses the area in front of docks 5-8. There are 4 outbound dock doors and outbound loads are not to be staged in Zone F.

9. Report any over-limit, damaged packaging or suspected leak in Zone F to the shift supervisor immediately and initiate PR-13 Hazmat handling and spill response. Do not attempt to move leaking containers without the correct PPE and containment.

title: Replenishment of Pick Faces
text:
1. Apply PR-03 Replenishment of pick faces to prepare all pick faces before any picking activity commences.
2. Complete replenishment BEFORE the picking shift starts.
3. Do not release picking tasks until the replenishment cycle is confirmed complete in the WMS.
4. Roles for this procedure:
  a. Forklift operators operate forklifts, reach trucks and pallet jacks to move full pallets from bulk storage to the picking zone.
  b. Pickers pick customer orders in Zone C against scanner tasks only after replenishment is complete.
5. Source stock:
  a. Identify replenishment requirements from WMS low-stock alerts for Zone C.
  b. Collect required pallets from Zone B, which is the bulk storage zone with high-bay pallet racking.
  c. Verify pallet label, product code and quantity against the scanner task before movement.
6. Replenish Zone C:
  a. Transport pallets to Zone C, which is the picking zone with ground-level pick faces and flow racks.
  b. Place stock into the designated pick face or flow rack lane as directed by the scanner.
  c. Confirm placement with a scanner scan to update inventory location in real time.
  d. Remove empty pallets and return them to the designated collection point.
7. Equipment use:
  a. Use handheld WMS scanners to drive every move. Pickers and inbound staff share 20 handheld WMS scanners; reserve sufficient units for the replenishment team at shift start.
  b. Report any scanner fault to the shift supervisor immediately and obtain a replacement unit before continuing.
8. Movement and safety:
  a. Travel via main transport aisles where available. Main transport aisles are 4.0 m wide.
  b. Enter rack storage aisles only when required for put-away. Rack storage aisles are 3.0 m wide.
  c. Observe forklift speed limits at all times. Forklifts must not exceed 8 km/h inside the building.
  d. Give way to pedestrians at all marked crossings and maintain clear sightlines at aisle intersections.
9. Completion checks:
  a. Confirm every pick face listed on the replenishment wave shows green on the scanner.
  b. Re-queue any short replenishments due to missing stock and escalate to the shift supervisor.
  c. Hand over Zone C to the picking team only when the WMS confirms replenishment is complete.

title: Order Picking in Zone C
text:
1. Purpose and scope
This instruction defines PR-04 Order picking in Zone C. It applies to all picking of customer orders from ground-level pick faces and flow racks.

2. Zone and tasking
1. Perform all picking activity only in Zone C. Zone C is the picking zone comprising ground-level pick faces and flow racks.
2. Pick customer orders in Zone C against WMS scanner tasks. Do not pick from paper lists or verbal instructions.
3. Log onto the WMS with your personal ID and accept the next scanner-directed task. Complete tasks in WMS sequence unless the shift supervisor reprioritises.
4. Pickers own picking execution against scanner tasks. The shift supervisor runs the shift and resolves exceptions on the floor.

3. Pre-start conditions
1. Verify that PR-03 Replenishment of pick faces is complete. Pick faces are replenished before the picking shift starts; do not commence PR-04 Order picking while replenishment is still in progress.
2. Collect a serviceable handheld WMS scanner. Pickers and inbound staff share 20 handheld WMS scanners; return the unit to the charging station when the task batch is complete.
3. Wear mandatory personal protective equipment before entering the warehouse floor. High-visibility vests are mandatory for everyone on the warehouse floor. Safety footwear class S3 is mandatory on the warehouse floor.

4. Picking execution
1. Travel to the location directed by the scanner. Confirm the location label by scanning.
2. Pick the exact product, batch and quantity displayed. Scan each unit barcode as prompted.
3. Place picked items directly into the assigned tote or order carton. Do not consolidate multiple orders into a single tote.
4. If stock is missing, damaged or short, use the scanner exception code and leave the location as found. Do not substitute alternative stock.
5. Report any empty or low pick face to the shift supervisor for replenishment via PR-03 Replenishment of pick faces.

5. Scan verification and transfer to packing
1. Complete scan verification before packing. Picked items are scan-verified before packing under PR-04 Order picking and PR-05 Packing and labelling.
2. At the end of the pick path, confirm the tote with the scanner close function. The WMS will release the tote for PR-05 Packing and labelling only after verification succeeds.
3. Place verified totes onto the designated outbound conveyor or transfer trolley for Zone C. Do not stage unverified totes.

6. Movement in Zone C
1. Observe forklift and pallet jack traffic rules while picking. Forklifts must not exceed 8 km/h inside the building.
2. Forklifts must slow to 5 km/h in marked pedestrian zones and crossings. Give way to pedestrians at all marked crossings in Zone C.
3. Keep pick aisles clear of empty pallets and shrink wrap. Return handling equipment to its lane after use.

title: Scan Verification
text:
1. Apply scan verification to every order completed under PR-04 Order picking before starting PR-05 Packing and labelling.
   Zone C is the picking zone: ground-level pick faces and flow racks. Hold all unverified picks inside Zone C until verification passes.

2. Assign verification only to trained pickers.
   Pickers pick customer orders in Zone C against scanner tasks. Instruct each picker to scan-verify their own picks and not delegate verification to other staff.

3. Observe the mandatory sequence for PR-04 Order picking and PR-05 Packing and labelling.
   Scan-verify picked items BEFORE packing. Do not apply cartons, labels, tape or wrap to any order that has not achieved WMS verification acceptance.

4. Operate verification with handheld WMS scanners.
   Pickers and inbound staff share 20 handheld WMS scanners. Collect a scanner at shift start, check battery level and check scanner strap and screen condition.

5. Execute the scan at the pick face or adjacent mobile station.
   Scan the order or tote barcode first, then scan each item barcode individually. Enter quantity on the scanner when prompted and wait for the WMS acceptance tone and green confirmation.

6. Handle mismatches as immediate stops.
   On a reject tone, red screen or quantity variance, halt packing for that order. Re-count the physical items, check the product code against the task screen, and rescan. Segregate the tote if the mismatch persists.

7. Escalate unresolved exceptions before transfer.
   Notify the shift supervisor and stock controller of any persistent scan failure. Keep the affected tote in Zone C. Do not move it to Zone D.

8. Transfer only verified orders to packing and staging.
   Upon WMS confirmation, close the verification step on the scanner to complete PR-04 Order picking. WMS then releases the order to PR-05 Packing and labelling for packing, labelling and wrapping.

9. Stage verified orders in the dispatch zone.
   Zone D is the dispatch zone: outbound staging in front of docks 5-8. Place verified and packed cartons in the assigned Zone D lane facing the allocated outbound dock.

10. Maintain scanner control and traceability.
    Return the 20 shared scanners to charging bays at break and shift end. Log any damaged or low-battery unit and obtain a replacement before resuming picking. Retain WMS verification logs for audit and incident review.

title: Packing, Labelling and Wrapping in Zone D
text:
1. Scope and control. This section governs PR-05 Packing and labelling and the transfer to PR-06 Outbound dispatch. Complete PR-05 in full before releasing any load under PR-06.

2. Location. Perform all packing, labelling and wrapping in Zone D. Zone D is the dispatch zone: outbound staging in front of docks 5-8. Do not pack or stage outbound loads at other doors; dock doors 5-8 serve outbound dispatch.

3. Separation from value-added work. Keep standard dispatch packing in Zone D only. Zone F holds the value-added services area for rework, kitting and other non-standard activities. Move a unit to Zone F only when a value-added instruction applies.

4. Personal protective equipment. Wear required PPE at all times on the warehouse floor in Zone D:
   a) High-visibility vests are mandatory for everyone on the warehouse floor.
   b) Safety footwear class S3 is mandatory on the warehouse floor.
   Do not enter packing lanes without both items.

5. Verification before packing. Apply the fixed sequence for PR-05. Picked items are scan-verified BEFORE packing. Complete scan verification, resolve any short or mismatch, and only then start packing and labelling. Never pack unverified picks.

6. Packing and labelling instructions:
   a) Check the order and carton against the WMS task.
   b) Select the correct carton, pallet or tote for the order profile.
   c) Apply the customer label, carrier label and any handling label straight, fully adhered and scannable. Ensure barcodes face outward.
   d) Seal cartons and secure goods to prevent movement in transit.

7. Pallet building and weight limit. Build stable, stackable pallets in Zone D outbound staging.
   a) A pallet, including its load, may weigh at most 900 kg. Do not exceed this limit for any pallet released to dispatch.
   b) Distribute weight evenly, keep the footprint within the pallet, and use interlayer sheets where required.
   c) Rebuild any unstable or overweight pallet before wrapping.

8. Stretch wrapping. Wrap every outbound pallet prior to staging:
   a) Dispatch uses 2 semi-automatic stretch wrappers in Zone D. Queue pallets to the next available wrapper; do not wrap by hand where a wrapper is specified.
   b) Apply the prescribed wrap pattern and containment force for the load type.
   c) Inspect the finished wrap for tears, exposed corners or loose tails. Rewrap defective loads.

9. Waste and housekeeping. Flatten all scrap cartons immediately and feed them to the site baler. The site has 1 cardboard baler. Keep Zone D aisles, wrappers and staging lanes clear of loose cardboard, banding and film.

10. Staging for PR-06. After wrapping, place labelled pallets in the allocated outbound staging lane in Zone D in dock-door sequence. Confirm door assignment for docks 5-8 and load number with PR-06 documentation before moving pallets to the dock. Do not block levellers or pedestrian routes while staging.

title: Staging and Load Release
text:
1. Stage only finished pallets in Zone D. Place outbound pallets only in the outbound staging area in front of docks 5-8.

Zone D is the dispatch zone: outbound staging in front of docks 5-8. Do not use Zone D for picking, replenishment or returns staging. Keep staging lanes clear of empty pallets and packing waste.

2. Confirm PR-06 requirements are met before staging. Complete PR-05 Packing and labelling in full before any load is released under PR-06 Outbound dispatch.

Check each pallet is stretch-wrapped and carries its correct outbound label. Do not move pallets to staging if wrapping is incomplete or labels are missing. Reject any pallet that has not passed verification and return it to Zone D packing for correction.

3. Obtain dispatcher assignment for every load. The dispatcher books transport, assigns dock doors and releases outbound loads.

Do not move staged pallets to the dock without an assigned door and time slot from the dispatcher. The dispatcher assigns dock doors and time slots to carriers; follow the assigned slot and door exactly.

4. Confirm door assignment before moving to the dock. Dock doors 5-8 serve outbound dispatch.

Request confirmation of the specific door among docks 5-8 for the load. Move pallets to the dock only after door confirmation. Stage in the lane that feeds the confirmed door and keep other door approaches clear.

5. Prepare the dock leveller at the assigned door. Each of the 8 dock doors has a dock leveller.

Inspect the leveller and dock approach before travel. Ensure the leveller is seated, locked to the trailer bed and rated for the load. Report any defect to the shift supervisor and do not use a faulty leveller.

6. Obey speed limits when handling staged loads. Forklifts must not exceed 8 km/h inside the building.

Slow to 5 km/h in marked pedestrian zones and crossings. Give way to pedestrians at all marked crossings. Approach staging lanes and outbound lanes at low speed and sound the horn where sight lines are restricted.

7. Observe the dock ramp limit. Forklifts must not exceed 5 km/h on dock ramps and leveller approaches.

Align straight to the leveller, carry the load low and travel at creep speed onto the ramp. Do not brake sharply or turn on the leveller plate. Stop and re-align if the pallet overhangs the forks.

8. Release the load only after checks are complete. Under PR-06 a load may only be released after loading and door checks are complete.

Load in the sequence stated on the assignment and secure each row before moving the next. Notify the dispatcher once loading and door checks are complete so the dispatcher can release the outbound load. Leave the staging area clear for the next confirmed load.

title: Vehicle Loads and Outbound Capacity
text:
1. Execute all outbound movements under PR-06 Outbound dispatch from Zone D.

All loading, door moves and vehicle releases for PR-06 Outbound dispatch are performed from Zone D. Do not stage or release outbound loads from any other zone.

2. Use only docks 5-8 for outbound dispatch. The site provides 4 outbound dock doors for this purpose.

Dock doors 5-8 serve outbound dispatch. The dispatcher assigns dock doors and time slots to carriers and confirms door numbers before any pallet is moved to the dock.

3. Obtain the dispatcher's confirmed door assignment before transferring any pallet to the dock. Do not move loads to docks 5-8 without that confirmation.

Hold pallets in Zone D staging until the dispatcher has communicated the assigned door to the shift supervisor, forklift operators and carrier. Move to the dock only after that confirmation is recorded.

4. Verify PR-05 Packing and labelling is completed in full before release under PR-06 Outbound dispatch. Stage only stretch-wrapped pallets in Zone D.

PR-05 Packing and labelling must be completed in full before any load is released under PR-06 Outbound dispatch. Every outbound pallet must be stretch-wrapped prior to placement in outbound staging. Do not stage unwrapped pallets.

5. Observe the pallet limit: a pallet, including its load, may weigh at most 900 kg. Check gross weight on the scanner record before assigning vehicle type.

A pallet, including its load, may weigh at most 900 kg. Weigh-check any pallet suspected to be overweight. Report any overweight pallet or over-limit staging to the shift supervisor immediately.

6. Load contracted curtain-side trailers within both limits:
   a. Payload limit is 26000 kg.
   b. Floor capacity is 33 pallet positions.
   c. At maximum pallet weight, payload governs capacity. A trailer takes at most 28 full-weight pallets (payload divided by maximum pallet weight, capped by floor positions).

Do not exceed either the payload limit or the floor positions. For full-weight pallets, plan to a maximum of 28 pallets per trailer.

7. Load the delivery van within both limits:
   a. Payload limit is 1800 kg.
   b. Floor capacity is 6 pallet positions.
   c. At maximum pallet weight, the van takes at most 2 full-weight pallets. Route any heavier order by trailer.

Check both weight and floor positions before assigning the van. If the order exceeds 2 full-weight pallets, book trailer capacity and do not split a full-weight pallet across vehicles.

8. Plan door utilisation per shift. Each outbound door handles 4 trailer loads per shift.

Coordinate with the dispatcher to sequence bookings across the 4 outbound doors. Keep each door to its planned 4 loads per shift and avoid queuing trailers outside the assigned time slots.

9. Calculate outbound capacity on full-weight pallets. With 4 doors each handling 4 loads of 28 pallets, outbound capacity is at most 448 full-weight pallets per shift (doors x loads per shift x pallets per trailer). Schedule bookings within that ceiling and refer overflow to the next shift. Adding trailer capacity beyond the 448 full-weight pallet per shift limit requires warehouse manager agreement.

Do not exceed the calculated ceiling without prior agreement. Record all bookings in the WMS and refer excess demand to the next available shift.

10. Respect hazmat constraints when staging mixed loads. No more than 3,000 kg of hazmat may be stored in the hazmat cage inside Zone F at one time. At maximum pallet weight this equates to at most 3 full-weight pallets (hazmat stock limit divided by maximum pallet weight). Do not allocate hazmat pallets to a trailer until cage stock is confirmed within limit.

Stage hazmat only inside the hazmat cage in Zone F. Confirm the cage total is within limit before building any outbound hazmat load.

11. Record trailer and van loads, door numbers and pallet counts in the WMS before releasing the vehicle. Report any overweight pallet or over-limit staging to the shift supervisor immediately.

Trailer and van loads, door numbers and pallet counts must be recorded in the WMS before the vehicle is released. Do not release until the dispatcher has verified the record and loading and door checks are complete.

title: Aisle Network and Walkways
text:
1. Maintain physical separation between pedestrians and trucks at all times in accordance with PR-11 Pedestrian safety in the warehouse.

Keep main transport aisles free of staging, pallets and waste. Main transport aisles are 4.0 m wide and provide two-way truck circulation between zones.

2. Use rack storage aisles only for put-away, replenishment and picking access.

Rack storage aisles are 3.0 m wide. Do not park or stage pallets inside these aisles except during active handling at the bay face.

3. Walk only inside segregated pedestrian walkways when moving between zones.

Segregated pedestrian walkways are 1.2 m wide and are marked with solid floor lines and hatched crossings. Do not step outside the walkway to take shortcuts across truck routes.

4. Follow the marked network that connects all operational zones.

Zone A is the receiving zone: inbound docks 1-4, unloading and goods inspection. Zone B is the bulk storage zone: high-bay pallet racking. Zone C is the picking zone: ground-level pick faces and flow racks. Zone D is the dispatch zone: outbound staging in front of docks 5-8.

Cross between these zones only at designated pedestrian crossings. Yield to trucks at every intersection.

5. Keep walkways and aisle markings visible and unobstructed.

Report faded paint, damaged barriers or blocked sightlines to the shift supervisor immediately. Do not place bins, roll cages or packing materials on walkway edges.

6. Wear required personal protective equipment on the warehouse floor.

High-visibility vests are mandatory for everyone on the warehouse floor. Wear them fully fastened and keep them clean so you remain visible in aisles and crossings.

7. Observe priority rules where walkways intersect truck aisles.

Stop at the crossing line and check both directions before proceeding. Make eye contact with the operator where possible and wait until the truck has passed.

8. Protect pedestrian routes during peak movements.

When staging outbound pallets or feeding Zone C pick faces, keep loads inside the bay footprint and never encroach on the 1.2 m walkway. If a walkway must be temporarily closed for maintenance, install barriers and diversion signs and inform all operators on shift.

title: Speed Limits
text:
1. Apply the limits in this section at all times when operating forklifts, reach trucks and pallet jacks under PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation. Pedestrians and operators share the same aisles and must work to PR-11 Pedestrian safety in the warehouse.

2. Do not exceed 8 km/h inside the building. This ceiling applies to every indoor area, including Zones A, B, C, D, E and F, and to all main and storage aisles.

3. Do not exceed 12 km/h in the outdoor yard. Reduce speed further when the yard is congested, when visibility is restricted, or when the surface is wet or uneven.

4. Slow to 5 km/h in marked pedestrian zones and at every pedestrian crossing. Give way to pedestrians on the segregated walkways and at aisle intersections.

5. Do not exceed 5 km/h on dock ramps and leveller approaches at doors 1-8. Approach the leveller squarely, keep the forks low, and stop if the leveller plate is not fully seated.

6. Observe signage and floor markings at all zone transitions. If a lower limit is posted, follow the posted limit. Never use the outdoor limit indoors, and never use the indoor limit in pedestrian zones or on dock ramps.

7. Report any speeding, near miss or collision immediately to the shift supervisor on duty. Stop the truck safely, secure the load, and preserve the scene for inspection.

8. The shift supervisor reviews every incident report. Provide the time, location, truck identification, load status and witness details to support the review under PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation.

9. Enforce these limits through daily supervision, scanner and WMS route discipline, and the documented pre-use check required by PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation. Treat repeated non-compliance as a safety breach under PR-11 Pedestrian safety in the warehouse and remove the operator from MHE duties pending re-briefing.

10. Keep this section displayed with PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation and PR-11 Pedestrian safety in the warehouse at the MHE charging area and at each dock office so that indoor, outdoor, pedestrian zone and dock ramp limits remain visible on every shift.

title: Pedestrian Safety Rules
text:
1. Apply PR-11 Pedestrian safety in the warehouse on every entry to the warehouse floor.
2. Wear a high-visibility vest at all times on the warehouse floor. Do not enter or remain on the floor without it fastened and visible.
3. Wear safety footwear class S3 at all times on the warehouse floor. Replace damaged or non-compliant footwear before starting work.
4. Stay inside the marked pedestrian system. Keep to the segregated pedestrian walkways. These walkways are 1.2 m wide and are bounded by barriers and floor markings.
5. Stop at every pedestrian crossing and barrier gate. Make eye contact with the forklift operator and wait for the truck to halt before stepping out.
6. Never walk under raised forks or a raised load. Never climb on racking or dock levellers to pass a vehicle.
7. Observe forklift speed discipline at all times:
 a) Forklifts must not exceed 8 km/h inside the building.
 b) Forklifts must slow to 5 km/h in marked pedestrian zones and crossings. Expect trucks to be moving at this reduced speed and keep clear.
 c) Forklifts must not exceed 5 km/h on dock ramps and leveller approaches. Do not overtake or crowd trucks on ramps.
8. Keep pedestrian walkways clear. Do not stage pallets, cages, stretch wrap or waste in the 1.2 m walkways or across crossing sight lines. Return barriers and gates to the closed position after use.
9. Use designated pedestrian doors where provided. Do not use dock doors or vehicle aisles as shortcuts. Where a pedestrian must cross a vehicle aisle, use only the marked crossing.
10. Obey all audible and visual warnings. Stop when you hear a forklift horn or reverse alarm. Yield to forklifts, reach trucks and pallet jacks at all times.
11. Report every near miss, collision, trip or barrier damage immediately. The shift supervisor runs one shift: floor staff and incident response, and reviews every incident report. Provide the location, time and vehicles or persons involved.
12. Cooperate with temporary controls during spills, rack repairs or evacuation drills. Follow the shift supervisor's instructions and any additional barriers, signs or spotters put in place under PR-11 Pedestrian safety in the warehouse.

title: Electric Fleet
text:
1. Fleet inventory for internal transport is fixed and fully electric for powered trucks. Do not exceed rated capacities or site weight limits when planning lifts and storage.

2. Counterbalance forklifts: the fleet has 9 electric counterbalance forklifts. Each unit is rated at 3.0 t. Use these trucks for dock work, yard movements and bulk transport between zones.

3. Reach trucks: the fleet has 5 reach trucks for the high bays. Each reach truck is rated at 2.0 t. Reserve reach trucks for racking operations in the high-bay areas where height and aisle width require them.

4. Electric pallet jacks: the fleet has 11 electric pallet jacks. Assign these units to horizontal movements of full pallets, replenishment support and outbound staging.

5. Hand pallet jacks: the site has 12 hand pallet jacks. Keep these units distributed across receiving, picking and dispatch for short moves and manual handling where powered equipment is not required.

6. Personnel authorised to operate this equipment are defined by role. Forklift operators operate forklifts, reach trucks and pallet jacks. No other role may operate MHE unless authorised separately.

7. Pallet weight limit applies to every load moved by any truck. A pallet, including its load, may weigh at most 900 kg. Check the declared weight in the WMS before lifting and reject any pallet stated above this limit for standard handling.

8. Racking load limit applies to every bay in bulk storage. Each rack bay may carry at most 2,700 kg. Calculate total bay load from pallet weights and pallet positions before put-away and do not exceed the bay rating.

9. Hazmat storage limit applies to the cage in Zone F. No more than 3,000 kg of hazmat may be stored in the hazmat cage at one time. Monitor cumulative hazmat weight on receipt and during put-away to remain within the cage limit.

10. Handheld WMS scanners support all moves. Pickers and inbound staff share 20 handheld WMS scanners. Book equipment out at shift start and return units to charge at shift end; report faults to the shift supervisor immediately.

11. Match truck to task by weight and location. Use counterbalance trucks for general transport, reach trucks for high-bay placement, and pallet jacks for low-level moves. Never substitute a lower-rated truck to lift a load beyond its rating.

12. Maintain availability through correct charging and parking. Park powered trucks in designated charging lanes at breaks and at end of shift. Keep hand pallet jacks clear of aisles and pedestrian walkways when not in use.

title: Authorisation and Daily Checks
text:
1. This section applies PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation to authorisation and daily checks for all powered MHE.
2. The fleet covered comprises 9 electric counterbalance forklifts, 5 reach trucks for the high bays and 11 electric pallet jacks.
3. Only the warehouse manager may authorise new forklift operators.
4. Do not operate any counterbalance forklift, reach truck or electric pallet jack without current authorisation under PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation.
5. Present licence, training certificate and authorisation record for verification before first assignment.
6. The warehouse manager is accountable for the whole site: operations, safety and final sign-offs, including all authorisations under PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation.
7. Retain the signed authorisation on file and revoke operating rights immediately when training lapses or following unsafe operation.
8. Complete the documented pre-use check for every forklift each day.
9. Perform the daily forklift check BEFORE first use each day in accordance with PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation.
10. Do not start the truck until the daily check is fully recorded and passed.
11. Inspect brakes, steering, tyres/wheels, forks, chains, mast, lights, horn, reversing alarm and emergency stop where fitted.
12. Test battery charge, connections and electrolyte indicators on electric trucks and confirm isolation switches function correctly.
13. Record defects on the daily check sheet and tag the truck out of service if any safety-critical fault is found.
14. Report the defect to the shift supervisor and notify the maintenance technician without delay.
15. The maintenance technician maintains MHE, racking and dock equipment and logs all repairs.
16. Do not attempt field repairs; await release by the maintenance technician after the repair log entry.
17. File completed daily check sheets in the MHE control file for audit and retain in shift order.
18. Apply the same daily documented check discipline to reach trucks and electric pallet jacks before first use.

title: Safe Operation
text:
1. Follow PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation for every truck movement inside the building, in the outdoor yard and on dock ramps and leveller approaches.

2. Restrict driving to authorised personnel only. Forklift operators operate forklifts, reach trucks and pallet jacks; no other role may operate MHE.

3. Fasten the seat belt before the truck moves. Forklift operators must wear seat belts whenever the truck is moving, including short repositioning and inching to a rack face.

4. Observe rated capacities when planning lifts. Counterbalance forklifts are rated at 3.0 t and reach trucks are rated at 2.0 t; do not exceed the rated capacity for the truck in use.

5. Control speed to the posted limit for the area. Inside the building, forklifts must not exceed 8 km/h.

6. In the outdoor yard, reduce speed appropriately but forklifts must not exceed 12 km/h.

7. At any marked pedestrian zone or crossing, slow further. Forklifts must slow to 5 km/h in marked pedestrian zones and crossings and give way to pedestrians.

8. Apply the same low-speed limit on dock infrastructure. Forklifts must not exceed 5 km/h on dock ramps and leveller approaches; approach squarely and check that the leveller is fully seated before crossing.

9. Use the aisle network as marked. Main transport aisles are 4.0 m wide and provide two-way travel for forklifts and pallet jacks.

10. Enter rack storage aisles only when clear. Rack storage aisles are 3.0 m wide; keep forks low while travelling, sound the horn at blind intersections and stop for oncoming trucks.

11. Keep aisles free of obstructions. Do not stage pallets, waste or charging equipment in main aisles or storage aisles, and maintain clear sightlines at aisle ends and pedestrian crossings.

12. Report defects immediately and withdraw the truck from service until cleared. Record any rack strike, wheel damage or leveller fault and notify the shift supervisor, as racking gets a documented safety inspection every month and strikes must be logged for that inspection.

title: Returns Intake and Inspection
text:
1. Apply PR-07 Returns handling to every customer return arriving at Harborwick 3PL Ltd.

2. Accept returns only within 14 days of delivery. Reject any return outside this window and record the delivery date, return date and reason for refusal in the WMS.

3. Receive returns through Zone A at dock doors 1-4, which serve inbound receiving. Do not receive returns through Zone D, which is the dispatch zone for outbound staging in front of docks 5-8.

4. Transfer the sealed return immediately to Zone F, which holds the value-added services area. Returns are inspected in Zone F and must not be inspected in any other zone.

5. Note that the hazmat cage is inside Zone F. Segregate any return marked as hazmat, leaking or odorous and place it adjacent to the hazmat cage for specialist assessment. Do not open hazmat returns on the general inspection bench.

6. Assign inspection to returns staff. Returns staff inspect returns in Zone F and propose restock, rework or scrap.

Duty list for returns staff under PR-07:
1) verify the return against the original delivery and the 14-day acceptance window;
2) open, count and examine condition, completeness and packaging;
3) photograph damage and retain labels;
4) propose one disposition: restock, rework or scrap.

7. Follow the mandatory sequence for PR-07. Returns are inspected BEFORE any restock, rework or scrap decision. Do not propose, select or execute a disposition until inspection is complete and documented.

8. Record the inspection outcome in the WMS before moving goods. Keep the physical return in Zone F until the disposition is approved and posted. Do not move inspected returns to bulk storage, picking or dispatch staging prior to approval.

9. Escalate any return that cannot be identified, is contaminated, or presents a safety risk. Hold the goods in Zone F and notify the shift supervisor for instruction.

title: Disposition and Write-Offs
text:
1. Apply this section to every decision made under PR-07 Returns handling and PR-09 Damaged-goods handling after inspection is complete.

2. Hold all goods awaiting a disposition decision in the quarantine area in Zone F. Do not move goods to bulk storage, picking or dispatch while the decision is pending.

3. Keep the quarantine area segregated within Zone F, which holds the value-added services area, and maintain clear identification of each pallet or unit under review.

4. Returns staff inspect returns in Zone F and propose restock, rework or scrap. Record the proposal in the WMS with the inspection notes and photographs.

5. Returns are inspected BEFORE any restock, rework or scrap decision. Do not action the proposal until inspection is closed and the proposal is logged.

6. The shift supervisor approves the final disposition of inspected returns under PR-07 Returns handling. Obtain that approval before releasing goods from quarantine.

7. Execute the approved disposition exactly as instructed:
  a. Restock approved goods to the assigned storage location.
  b. Route rework goods to the designated work area in Zone F.
  c. Move scrap goods to the scrap holding point and book the write-off in the WMS.

8. Process damaged goods under PR-09 Damaged-goods handling through quarantine in the same way. Segregate the damage, count and photograph it, and enter the estimated value.

9. Damaged-goods write-offs above 750 EUR need warehouse-manager approval. Damaged-goods write-offs up to 750 EUR are approved by the shift supervisor.

10. Submit write-off requests as follows:
  a. For write-offs up to 750 EUR, the shift supervisor reviews the evidence and approves or rejects the write-off in the WMS.
  b. For write-offs above 750 EUR, the shift supervisor endorses the request and forwards it to the warehouse manager, who is accountable for the whole site: operations, safety and final sign-offs, for final decision.

11. The shift supervisor runs one shift: floor staff and incident response, and retains control of quarantine releases during that shift. Do not bypass the shift supervisor for returns disposition or for damaged-goods write-offs within the 750 EUR limit.

12. Only the warehouse manager may sign off stocktake results. Do not apply that authority to returns or damaged-goods decisions, which follow the thresholds in this section.

title: Cycle Counting
text:
1. Execute PR-08 Stocktaking and cycle counts for cycle counting on every working day. Follow the rotating zone schedule without omission.

2. Stock controllers own inventory accuracy: cycle counts, recounts and adjustments. Apply that duty throughout PR-08.

3. Count daily across all storage areas:
   a. Zone B is the bulk storage zone: high-bay pallet racking.
   b. Zone C is the picking zone: ground-level pick faces and flow racks.
   c. Zone E is the cold zone: chilled storage held at +2 to +6 °C.
   d. Zone F holds the value-added services area.

4. Plan the rotating zone schedule so each zone is counted in rotation. Issue count tasks in the WMS at shift start and assign a stock controller as count owner.

5. Perform counts with handheld WMS scanners. Pickers and inbound staff share 20 handheld WMS scanners; coordinate scanner allocation with the shift supervisor to maintain coverage of PR-08 counts alongside receiving and picking.

6. Scan each location and product systematically. Do not post any adjustment from the first count alone.

7. Investigate every variance immediately:
   a. Check adjacent locations, overstock, and recent put-away or replenishment moves.
   b. Verify against inbound receipts, pick tasks and dispatch staging.
   c. For Zone E, verify the location while maintaining the +2 to +6 °C condition and report any temperature excursion separately.

8. Execute the recount rule: a second count happens BEFORE any stock adjustment is posted (PR-08). Assign the recount to a second checker where possible and record both results in the WMS.

9. Hold adjustments until verified. After the recount, present unresolved variances to the warehouse manager for review. Only the warehouse manager may sign off stocktake results and authorise the posting of adjustments.

10. Post approved adjustments in the WMS with reason code, location, product, quantity, counter names and approval reference. Retain scanner logs and recount sheets with the PR-08 record.

11. Close the daily cycle count in the WMS, update the rotating zone schedule, and handover outstanding variances to the next shift stock controller.

title: Annual Wall-to-Wall Stocktake
text:
1. Apply PR-08 Stocktaking and cycle counts for this wall-to-wall count across the full site.
2. A full wall-to-wall stocktake runs once a year and covers the entire inventory holding of the warehouse.
3. The count covers the warehouse floor which covers 6,000 m2, including all racking, bulk, picking, cold and quarantine locations.
4. Roles and accountability for PR-08 are:
   a) The warehouse manager is accountable for the whole site: operations, safety and final sign-offs.
   b) Stock controllers own inventory accuracy: cycle counts, recounts and adjustments.
5. Prepare for shutdown:
   a) Freeze all inbound, outbound and internal movements for the count window.
   b) Clear work-in-progress from aisles and confirm all pallets are in a defined location.
   c) Issue count sheets, scanners and zone assignments to counting teams.
6. Execute the count:
   a) Count every pallet position, pick face and floor location by zone in sequence.
   b) Record counts directly in the WMS or on controlled count sheets where directed.
   c) Keep counting teams independent from the stockholding area they normally operate.
7. Control variances:
   a) Compare first count to system stock immediately after each zone is completed.
   b) Investigate any variance on the spot for obvious misplacements or labelling errors.
   c) A second count happens before any stock adjustment is posted.
   d) Assign the recount to a different counter than the first count and have the stock controller verify the result.
8. Post recount actions:
   a) Post adjustments only after the recount is confirmed.
   b) Log the reason code for every adjustment and retain supporting evidence with the count record.
   c) Reconcile the total inventory value and pallet quantity before closing the count.
9. Sign-off and close:
   a) Present the final variance report, recount evidence and adjustment log to the warehouse manager.
   b) Only the warehouse manager may sign off stocktake results.
   c) Do not release the system for normal operations until sign-off is recorded.
10. Retain the signed stocktake file, variance reports and adjustment audit trail for audit as directed by the warehouse manager.

title: Adjustments and Recounts
text:
1. Apply this section to every variance found during PR-08 Stocktaking and cycle counts. Treat cycle-count variances and full stocktake variances under the same control.

2. Execute a recount before any adjustment. A second count happens before any stock adjustment is posted. Do not post the adjustment from the first count alone.

3. Assign accountability for accuracy to the stock controller. Stock controllers own inventory accuracy: cycle counts, recounts and adjustments. Direct all count sheets, recount requests and system adjustments to the stock controller for verification.

4. Trigger recounts from daily cycle counts. Cycle counts run every working day on a rotating zone schedule. Raise a recount immediately when the first count does not match the system quantity, when the location holds damaged stock, or when the picker reports a short pick.

5. Isolate the location pending recount. Keep the pallet or bin on hold in the system. Do not move, pick, replenish or dispatch stock from that location until the recount is complete.

6. Perform the recount independently. Use the original count method and re-scan each item. Record the second quantity, the counter name and the time on the recount form and return it to the stock controller.

7. Verify and decide on adjustment. Instruct the stock controller to compare the first and second counts, investigate system movements, and determine the correct on-hand quantity. Post the stock adjustment in the WMS only after the recount result is verified.

8. Link stock adjustments that create damaged-goods write-offs to the approval threshold. Damaged-goods write-offs above 750 EUR need warehouse-manager approval.

9. Route write-off approvals as follows. Submit write-offs up to 750 EUR to the shift supervisor for approval. Submit write-offs above 750 EUR to the warehouse manager for approval. For damaged-goods write-offs above 750 EUR the shift supervisor must endorse the request and forward it to the warehouse manager for final decision. Do not scrap, donate or remove stock from the system without the applicable approval recorded.

10. Close stocktake results under final sign-off control. Only the warehouse manager may sign off stocktake results. Withhold system release and financial posting of annual stocktake adjustments until that sign-off is recorded for PR-08 Stocktaking and cycle counts.

title: Racking and Equipment Maintenance
text:
1. Maintain racking, MHE and dock equipment to a safe, serviceable standard. Keep all storage within rated limits and keep a complete record of inspections and repairs.
2. Assign the maintenance technician to maintain MHE, racking and dock equipment and to log all repairs. Do not operate damaged racking, levellers or trucks until the maintenance technician has inspected and cleared them.
3. Carry out a documented safety inspection of all racking every month. Include uprights, beams, bracing, base plates, anchors and beam locks in Zone B and any other racked locations.
4. Record the monthly inspection by bay, level and date. Photograph defects, grade the damage and tag the bay out of use where required. Enter the result in the repair log on the same day.
5. Log every repair against the original defect. State the fault found, parts fitted, date completed and name of the maintenance technician. Close the tag only when the repair is verified and the log is signed.
6. Enforce bay load limits at all times. Each rack bay may carry at most 2,700 kg. Do not exceed the posted bay label. Redistribute or offload overweight bays immediately and report the occurrence for correction.
7. Apply block-stack limits where pallets are free block-stacked outside racking. Free block-stacked pallets must not exceed 4.0 m in height and must not exceed 3 pallets high. Measure from floor to top of load. Restack any non-compliant stack before leaving the area.
8. Include MHE and dock equipment in the inspection cycle. The fleet has 9 electric counterbalance forklifts and the fleet has 5 reach trucks for the high bays; check steering, brakes, forks, chains, hydraulics and safety devices. Each of the 8 dock doors has a dock leveller; check leveller plates, lips, pits, controls and edge guards.
9. Coordinate MHE checks with PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation. Report defects found during daily checks under PR-10 to the maintenance technician without delay. Take unserviceable trucks out of service, isolate the keys and update the log.
10. Review the repair log at each monthly inspection. Verify that outstanding actions are closed, recurring damage is investigated and preventive measures are applied to protect racking and equipment.

title: Cold-Chain and Hazmat Response
text:
1. Apply PR-12 Cold-chain handling to every activity in Zone E. Zone E is the cold zone: chilled storage held at +2 to +6 °C.

2. Maintain the cold zone within its limits at all times. Keep the temperature at or above +2 °C. Keep the temperature at or below +6 °C.

3. Verify cold-zone temperature manually each shift. Record the reading, the time and the verifier on the shift log. Do not rely on automated monitoring alone.

4. Respond immediately to any temperature alarm or out-of-range reading under PR-12 Cold-chain handling:
   a) Recheck the reading at the calibrated display inside Zone E.
   b) Keep doors closed and restrict entry while the check is repeated.
   c) Notify the shift supervisor without delay. The shift supervisor runs one shift: floor staff and incident response.
   d) Hold affected stock inside Zone E and tag it pending decision.
   e) Do not move chilled goods to another zone until the shift supervisor authorises release.

5. Apply PR-13 Hazmat handling and spill response to all hazmat receipts, storage and movements. The hazmat cage is inside Zone F. The hazmat cage inside Zone F covers 60 m2.
