6. Observe storage limits for the hazmat cage. Store no more than 3,000 kg of hazmat in the hazmat cage at one time. Calculate capacity on full-weight pallets: a pallet, including its load, may weigh at most 900 kg, so the hazmat cage holds at most 3 full-weight pallets.

7. Stage hazmat only inside the cage. Do not exceed the floor limit. Keep incompatible classes segregated in accordance with PR-13 Hazmat handling and spill response safety data sheets.

8. Execute spill response under PR-13 Hazmat handling and spill response as follows:
   a) Stop work and alert nearby personnel.
   b) Notify the shift supervisor immediately for incident response.
   c) Ventilate the area and isolate the spill. Do not wash spills into drains.
   d) Don appropriate PPE and deploy the spill kit for the material class.
   e) Contain, absorb and collect the material for safe disposal. Log the incident, quantity and corrective action.

9. Record every PR-12 Cold-chain handling verification and every PR-13 Hazmat handling and spill response event in the WMS. Report any limit breach, equipment fault or stock at risk to the shift supervisor for follow-up.

title: Evacuation and Assembly
text:
1. Apply PR-14 Emergency evacuation to every evacuation of the 6,000 m2 warehouse floor.
1.1. Treat any alarm, smoke, spill or structural warning as an order to evacuate.
1.2. Stop all handling, racking and dock activity immediately.
1.3. Leave forklifts and MHE where safe, secured and switched off.

2. Responsibilities for evacuation remain fixed.
2.1. The warehouse manager is accountable for the whole site: operations, safety and final sign-offs.
2.2. The shift supervisor runs one shift: floor staff and incident response, and directs the evacuation on the floor.
2.3. Follow the shift supervisor's instructions for routes, exits and assembly.

3. Use segregated routes and obey pedestrian controls.
3.1. Move on foot to the nearest emergency exit; do not use forklifts for evacuation.
3.2. Keep to the segregated pedestrian walkways; these walkways are 1.2 m wide and must remain clear at all times.
3.3. Where forklifts are still moving to a safe stop, require them to slow to 5 km/h in marked pedestrian zones and crossings and to yield to evacuating personnel.
3.4. Do not stop to collect personal items or to close WMS tasks.
3.5. Assist visitors and contractors to the exits and report missing persons to the shift supervisor.

4. Assemble and complete roll call at the north fence.
4.1. Proceed directly to the assembly point at the north fence outside the building.
4.2. Stand clear of dock roads and emergency vehicle access.
4.3. Report your name and team to the shift supervisor for roll call.
4.4. Do not leave the assembly point until your name is recorded.

5. Control re-entry strictly.
5.1. Roll call at the assembly point happens BEFORE anyone re-enters the building.
5.2. Wait for the shift supervisor to confirm that the building is declared safe for re-entry.
5.3. Re-enter only when directed, by the designated exit route in reverse, and resume operations as instructed.

6. Practise and review performance.
6.1. Participate in the evacuation drill that runs every quarter under PR-14 Emergency evacuation.
6.2. Treat each drill as a live evacuation for timing, routes and roll call.
6.3. Report defects in exits, signage, lighting or walkways immediately after the drill.
6.4. The shift supervisor reviews every incident report arising from an evacuation or drill and assigns corrective actions.
6.5. Keep the signed drill record and incident reviews on file for audit.

chapter_title: Chapter 1 - Traffic Management: Forklifts and Pedestrians
title: 1.1 Speed Limits and Transport Routes
text:
1. Observe the site speed limits at all times under PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation and PR-11 Pedestrian safety in the warehouse.

2. Do not exceed 8 km/h inside the building. This limit applies to all forklift operators operating forklifts, reach trucks and pallet jacks on the 6,000 m2 warehouse floor.

3. Do not exceed 12 km/h in the outdoor yard. Reduce speed before entering the building and before any marked crossing.

4. Slow to 5 km/h in marked pedestrian zones and crossings. Give way to pedestrians on the segregated walkways and at every intersection.

5. Do not exceed 5 km/h on dock ramps and leveller approaches. Approach dock doors 1-4 and dock doors 5-8 square-on, check the leveller is seated, and stop if the door is not clear.

6. Wear seat belts whenever the truck is moving. Do not operate any truck without the belt fastened and adjusted.

7. Keep to the defined transport routes:
   7.1. Main transport aisles are 4.0 m wide. Use them for all longitudinal travel and for access to Zones A to F.
   7.2. Rack storage aisles are 3.0 m wide. Enter only when putting away or retrieving loads and keep forks trailing when empty.
   7.3. Segregated pedestrian walkways are 1.2 m wide. Do not drive, stop or stage pallets on walkways. Pedestrians must stay inside walkways where provided.

8. Respect dock discipline. The building has 8 dock doors. Dock doors 1-4 serve inbound receiving. Dock doors 5-8 serve outbound dispatch. Do not stage or travel against the assigned door flow.

9. Only authorised operators may drive. Only the warehouse manager may authorise new forklift operators. Do not allow untrained or unauthorised persons to operate forklifts, reach trucks or pallet jacks.

10. The shift supervisor runs one shift: floor staff and incident response. Report speeding, blocked aisles, damaged walkway markings or leveller faults to the shift supervisor immediately for correction under PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation.

chapter_title: Chapter 1 - Traffic Management: Forklifts and Pedestrians
title: 1.2 Segregated Pedestrian Walkways and Dock Discipline
text:
1. Apply PR-11 Pedestrian safety in the warehouse at all times on the warehouse floor. Keep to marked routes, obey signage and barriers, and never take shortcuts through operational areas.

2. Use only the segregated pedestrian walkways when moving on foot. Segregated pedestrian walkways are 1.2 m wide and are physically marked from MHE traffic.

3. Wear mandatory PPE on every movement through the warehouse floor. High-visibility vests are mandatory for everyone on the warehouse floor and safety footwear class S3 is mandatory on the warehouse floor.

4. Give way to materials handling equipment at every marked crossing. Stop, make eye contact with the operator and cross only when the aisle is clear.

5. Main transport aisles are 4.0 m wide and carry two-way truck traffic. Do not stand, stage pallets or congregate in main transport aisles.

6. Forklifts must slow to 5 km/h in marked pedestrian zones and crossings. Operators must sound the horn and check mirrors before entering any pedestrian interface.

7. Forklifts must not exceed 5 km/h on dock ramps and leveller approaches. Each of the 8 dock doors has a dock leveller; approach only when the leveller is fully set and the trailer is chocked.

8. The building has 8 dock doors. Dock doors 1-4 serve inbound receiving and dock doors 5-8 serve outbound dispatch.

9. Zone A is the receiving zone: inbound docks 1-4, unloading and goods inspection. Inbound operators unload, count and inspect inbound goods in Zone A and work only in released doors.

10. Zone D is the dispatch zone: outbound staging in front of docks 5-8. Do not enter outbound staging to collect loads without dispatcher confirmation.

11. The dispatcher assigns dock doors and time slots to carriers. Do not open a door, call a vehicle forward or change a bay without dispatcher instruction.

12. The shift supervisor runs one shift: floor staff and incident response. Report blocked walkways, damaged barriers, faulty levellers or unsafe dock discipline to the shift supervisor immediately for action.

chapter_title: Chapter 1 - Traffic Management: Forklifts and Pedestrians
title: 1.3 Forklift Authorisation and Daily Checks
text:
1. Authorisation control under PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation is absolute.
2. Only the warehouse manager may authorise new forklift operators. The warehouse manager is accountable for the whole site: operations, safety and final sign-offs.
3. Do not operate any truck unless you are an authorised forklift operator. Forklift operators operate forklifts, reach trucks and pallet jacks.
4. The permitted fleet is fixed. The site holds:
  4.1. 9 electric counterbalance forklifts rated at 3.0 t;
  4.2. 5 reach trucks for the high bays rated at 2.0 t;
  4.3. 11 electric pallet jacks;
  4.4. 12 hand pallet jacks.
5. Operate only the truck type you are authorised and trained to use. Check the rating plate before lifting. Never exceed the rated capacity.
6. Wear your seat belt whenever the truck is moving. Forklift operators must wear seat belts whenever the truck is moving.
7. Complete the documented pre-use check every day before first use.
  7.1. Every forklift gets a documented pre-use check each day.
  7.2. The daily forklift check happens before first use each day. Do not start the first job until the check is signed.
  7.3. Report any defect immediately and tag the truck out of service. Do not use a defective truck.
8. Report faults to the maintenance technician. The maintenance technician maintains MHE, racking and dock equipment and logs all repairs.
9. Keep trucks and pedestrian areas separate. Observe all speed limits and pedestrian controls defined in PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation and PR-11 Pedestrian safety in the warehouse.
10. Handheld WMS scanners are not MHE and do not confer driving authorisation. Pickers and inbound staff share 20 handheld WMS scanners for warehouse tasks only.

chapter_title: Chapter 2 - Personal Protection and Safety Accountability
title: 2.1 Mandatory PPE on the Warehouse Floor
text:
1. Wear the required personal protective equipment on all parts of the warehouse floor.

2. The rule applies across the entire 6,000 m2 warehouse floor without exception. Everyone on the floor must comply at all times, including visitors, contractors and office staff in transit. Do not enter the floor area without full PPE, even for a short task.

3. Mandatory items are:

   a) High-visibility vest. High-visibility vests are mandatory for everyone on the warehouse floor. Keep the vest fastened and visible. Do not cover it with coats or bags that obscure visibility.
   b) Safety footwear class S3. Safety footwear class S3 is mandatory on the warehouse floor. Wear fully laced, undamaged S3 boots or shoes. Do not wear trainers, low-cut shoes or any footwear below S3.

4. Replace damaged or non-compliant PPE immediately. Report defects to your supervisor and obtain a replacement before resuming work. Do not modify PPE.

5. Comply with PR-11 Pedestrian safety in the warehouse at all times while on foot. PR-11 Pedestrian safety in the warehouse defines walkways, crossings and interaction with mechanical handling equipment. Keep to designated routes and follow its requirements in addition to PPE.

6. Additional requirement for forklift operators:

   a) Fasten the seat belt whenever the truck is moving. Forklift operators must wear seat belts whenever the truck is moving. This applies to counterbalance forklifts, reach trucks and pallet jacks where a seat belt is fitted.
   b) Do not operate any truck without a functioning seat belt. Report faults immediately and remove the truck from service until repaired.
   c) Keep hi-visibility vest and S3 footwear on while operating. PPE remains mandatory inside the cab.

7. Accountability for compliance:

   a) The warehouse manager is accountable for the whole site: operations, safety and final sign-offs. That accountability includes setting and enforcing PPE standards on the warehouse floor.
   b) The shift supervisor runs one shift: floor staff and incident response. The shift supervisor enforces PPE on their shift, challenges non-compliance and directs incident response if PPE failure contributes to injury or near miss.

8. Supervisors must:

   a) Check PPE at shift start and during floor patrols.
   b) Stop work where PPE is missing or incorrect and instruct the person to leave the floor until compliant.
   c) Record repeated non-compliance as an incident for follow-up.

9. All personnel must:

   a) Arrive on the floor already wearing hi-visibility vest and S3 footwear.
   b) Keep PPE on until you have left the floor area completely.
   c) Notify the shift supervisor of any hazard that reduces PPE effectiveness, such as poor lighting, spills or obstructed walkways.

10. No exemption applies for heat, short duration or low activity. The 6,000 m2 floor is a live mechanical handling area at all times.

chapter_title: Chapter 2 - Personal Protection and Safety Accountability
title: 2.2 Roles and Supervision for Safety
text:
1. Site accountability
1.1 The warehouse manager is accountable for the whole site: operations, safety and final sign-offs.
1.2 The warehouse manager holds sole authority for the following:
  a) Approve overtime. Only the warehouse manager may approve overtime.
  b) Authorise new forklift operators. Only the warehouse manager may authorise new forklift operators under PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation.
1.3 No other role may exercise the authorities in 1.2. Escalate requests to the warehouse manager and await written approval before proceeding.

2. Shift supervision
2.1 The shift supervisor runs one shift: floor staff and incident response.
2.2 Shifts are rostered as:
  a) Shift 1 runs 06:00-14:00, Monday to Friday.
  b) Shift 2 runs 14:00-22:00, Monday to Friday.
2.3 The on-duty shift supervisor is the first point of contact for safety issues, rule breaches and emergency coordination during their shift.
2.4 The shift supervisor reviews every incident report. Submit all incident reports to the shift supervisor without delay and do not close an incident until that review is complete.
2.5 At every change of supervisor, apply PR-15 End-of-shift handover. Conduct the handover on the warehouse floor and ensure both outgoing and incoming supervisors are present.

3. Operating roles and duties
3.1 Forklift operators operate forklifts, reach trucks and pallet jacks.
  a) Operate equipment only in accordance with PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation.
  b) Do not operate any truck until authorised by the warehouse manager and briefed on PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation and PR-11 Pedestrian safety in the warehouse.
3.2 Dispatchers book transport, assign dock doors and release outbound loads.
  a) The dispatcher assigns dock doors and time slots to carriers.
  b) Carriers must follow the dispatcher’s door assignments and time slots for both inbound and outbound movements.
3.3 The maintenance technician maintains MHE, racking and dock equipment and logs all repairs.
  a) Report defects in forklifts, racking or dock equipment to the maintenance technician and the shift supervisor immediately.
  b) Do not use tagged or defective equipment. Return it to service only after the maintenance technician has completed and logged the repair.

4. Supervision of safe work
4.1 All personnel must comply with PR-11 Pedestrian safety in the warehouse when working on the warehouse floor or crossing transport routes.
4.2 Supervisors must enforce PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation and PR-11 Pedestrian safety in the warehouse at all times, intervene on unsafe acts, and record corrective actions.
4.3 Where overtime, forklift authorisation or final sign-offs are required, obtain approval from the warehouse manager before work starts. Where dock scheduling or outbound release is required, obtain confirmation from the dispatcher.

5. Compliance
5.1 Follow the instructions of the shift supervisor for incident response and daily task allocation.
5.2 Escalate any conflict between operational demands and safety requirements to the shift supervisor and, if unresolved, to the warehouse manager for final sign-off.

chapter_title: Chapter 3 - Restricted Zones: Cold, Hazmat and Safe Storage
title: 3.1 Cold Zone Work (Zone E)
text:
3.1 Cold Zone Work (Zone E)

1. Zone E is the cold zone: chilled storage held at +2 to +6 °C. This segregated chilled area operates inside the warehouse floor covering 6,000 m2 and is reserved solely for goods requiring continuous chilled storage. Apply PR-12 Cold-chain handling to every entry, movement and storage activity affecting Zone E.

2. Maintain the cold zone at or above +2 °C at all times. Check that doors close fully after each transit and never wedge or prop them open. Report any ice build-up, seal damage or prolonged door opening that could drive temperature below the lower limit.

3. Maintain the cold zone at or below +6 °C at all times. Treat any reading above this upper limit as a cold-chain deviation. Initiate the response required under PR-12 Cold-chain handling immediately and prevent further warm air ingress until the area has stabilised.

4. Verify temperature manually each shift. Observe the calibrated display inside Zone E, record the reading with time and initials in the shift log, and compare it against the +2 to +6 °C range. Escalate out-of-range results without delay and retain the record for traceability.

5. Minimise exposure and keep the chamber closed. Plan picks and put-away to reduce entries, enter only when the task is ready, and exit promptly after completion. Allow doors to self-close and confirm engagement before leaving the area.

6. Wear mandatory personal protection on every warehouse floor task, including all Zone E work. High-visibility vests are mandatory for everyone on the warehouse floor and must be fully fastened and visible before entry.

7. Wear safety footwear class S3 on the warehouse floor, including inside the cold zone. Inspect footwear for secure fastening and intact soles, and move carefully where condensation or moisture may make surfaces slippery.

8. Limit Zone E access to personnel trained in PR-12 Cold-chain handling. Inform the supervisor before entering for extended tasks and maintain visual or radio contact so assistance can be summoned. Do not use the cold zone for breaks, storage of ambient goods or non-chilled equipment.

9. The shift supervisor runs one shift: floor staff and incident response. Direct every temperature alarm, failed verification, access problem or incident inside Zone E to the shift supervisor for immediate review and coordinated response.

10. The warehouse manager is accountable for the whole site: operations, safety and final sign-offs. Refer repeated deviations, equipment faults, unresolved alarms and any cold-chain risk affecting product integrity to the warehouse manager for decision and sign-off.

11. Contain suspected breaches inside Zone E. Hold affected stock in place, tag it clearly as pending cold-chain decision, and prevent movement to other zones until authorised release is given under PR-12 Cold-chain handling.

chapter_title: Chapter 3 - Restricted Zones: Cold, Hazmat and Safe Storage
title: 3.2 Hazmat Cage and Spill Response (Zone F)
text:
1. Zone F holds the value-added services area. The hazmat cage is inside Zone F and covers 60 m2. The quarantine area is also in Zone F, separate from the cage.

2. Store hazmat only inside the hazmat cage in Zone F. Do not stage hazmat in receiving, bulk storage, picking or dispatch.

3. Do not exceed 3,000 kg of hazmat in the hazmat cage at one time. Check the current cage total in the WMS before booking any inbound hazmat for put-away.

4. Obey the pallet limit. A pallet, including its load, may weigh at most 900 kg. At this maximum weight the hazmat cage holds at most 3 full-weight pallets. Report any overweight pallet to the shift supervisor immediately and do not place it in the cage until approved.

5. Wear mandatory PPE on the warehouse floor at all times when handling or working near hazmat. High-visibility vests are mandatory for everyone on the warehouse floor. Safety footwear class S3 is mandatory on the warehouse floor.

6. Follow PR-13 Hazmat handling and spill response for all hazmat movements, segregation and spill response. Do not open, decant or rework hazmat outside the designated area in Zone F.

7. If a leak, spill or strong odour occurs, stop work and alert persons nearby. Notify the shift supervisor, ventilate and isolate the area, and keep all persons clear of the spill.

8. Do not attempt clean-up without correct PPE and equipment. Don PPE and deploy the spill kit only when authorised, then contain, absorb, collect and log the incident as directed under PR-13.

9. The warehouse manager is accountable for the whole site: operations, safety and final sign-offs. The warehouse manager retains final sign-off for hazmat storage arrangements and safety controls in Zone F.

10. The maintenance technician maintains MHE, racking and dock equipment and logs all repairs. Report any damage to the hazmat cage, bunding, signage or ventilation to the maintenance technician and the shift supervisor without delay, and do not use defective equipment.

chapter_title: Chapter 3 - Restricted Zones: Cold, Hazmat and Safe Storage
title: 3.3 Racking and Free Stacking Limits
text:
1. Apply these limits to all racking in Zone B and to any free block stack on the floor. No pallet, including its load, may weigh more than 900 kg.

2. Do not exceed the rack bay limit. Each rack bay may carry at most 2,700 kg. Check the bay load plate before placing pallets and count the gross weight of every pallet in the bay against this limit.

3. Because the maximum pallet weight is 900 kg, a bay loaded with full-weight pallets can hold no more than three pallets. Three pallets at 900 kg equals 2,700 kg and reaches the bay limit. Reduce the number of pallets or the weight per pallet to stay within the limit.

4. Observe equipment limits when handling stock for racking:
   a) Counterbalance forklifts are rated at 3.0 t.
   b) Reach trucks for the high bays are rated at 2.0 t.
   Do not use equipment beyond its rated capacity to place or retrieve pallets.

5. Respect free block-stacking limits where pallets are not racked:
   a) Free block-stacked pallets must not exceed 4.0 m in height.
   b) Free block-stacked pallets must not exceed 3 pallets high.
   Both limits apply at the same time. Stop stacking when either limit is reached. Stack only on a level, stable floor and interlock tiers where the product allows.

6. Zone B is the bulk storage zone: high-bay pallet racking. The high-bay racking provides 2,400 pallet positions. Use only designated pallet positions in Zone B and do not stage unracked pallets in rack aisles.

7. Keep aisles clear for safe transport and access:
   a) Main transport aisles are 4.0 m wide.
   b) Rack storage aisles are 3.0 m wide.
   Do not encroach on aisle markings with overhanging pallets, wrappers or staging. Maintain clear sightlines at aisle intersections.

8. Report any rack damage immediately. Do not load, unload or pass under a damaged bay. Segregate the bay and apply PR-09 Damaged-goods handling for any affected stock. Move damaged or suspect pallets to the quarantine process and do not return them to racking until inspected.

9. Maintain racking integrity through scheduled checks. Racking gets a documented safety inspection every month. Cooperate with the inspection and remove loads as directed to allow access.

10. The maintenance technician maintains MHE, racking and dock equipment and logs all repairs. Log every defect, impact and repair on the racking and equipment register and retain the record for review.

chapter_title: Chapter 4 - Incidents, Damage and Emergency Response
title: 4.1 Incident Reporting and Review
text:
1. Report any incident on the warehouse floor to the shift supervisor without delay. This includes injury, near miss, collision, product damage, spill or breach of PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation, PR-11 Pedestrian safety in the warehouse or PR-14 Emergency evacuation.

2. Stop the task and secure the area where safe to do so. Alert nearby colleagues and prevent further exposure. Do not move equipment involved in the incident until the shift supervisor has attended, unless leaving it creates immediate danger.

3. Contact the shift supervisor who runs one shift: floor staff and incident response. Provide location, time, persons involved and a brief description of what happened. If the injured person cannot call, any witness must make the report on their behalf.

4. The shift supervisor will attend the scene, take control of incident response for that shift and decide on first actions. Direct injured persons to first aid, isolate hazards, and suspend related work in the affected zone until the area is declared safe.

5. Complete the incident report in full before leaving site that shift. Record the names of all persons present, the equipment and procedure in use, and the immediate cause as observed. Attach photographs where relevant and sign and time the entry.

6. The shift supervisor reviews every incident report. The review must verify facts, interview witnesses separately, confirm which procedure applied, and record corrective actions with owners and due dates. No report is closed without this review.

7. Coverage applies across both operating periods. Shift 1 runs 06:00-14:00, Monday to Friday, and Shift 2 runs 14:00-22:00, Monday to Friday. The on-duty shift supervisor for the relevant shift owns response and review for incidents occurring in that window. Handover any open incident to the next shift supervisor with a clear status of actions taken and actions outstanding.

8. Escalate serious incidents immediately beyond shift review. The warehouse manager is accountable for the whole site: operations, safety and final sign-offs, and retains final sign-off on serious incident investigations, site-wide safety actions and any decision to resume full operations after a major event.

9. Do not resume normal work in the affected area until the shift supervisor confirms the corrective action is in place. Where the incident relates to forklift or pedestrian control, confirm that controls under PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation or PR-11 Pedestrian safety in the warehouse have been re-briefed. Where evacuation was triggered, follow PR-14 Emergency evacuation for re-entry control.

10. File the reviewed report and track corrective actions to completion. Retain records for audit and brief all affected staff on lessons learned at the next shift start.

chapter_title: Chapter 4 - Incidents, Damage and Emergency Response
title: 4.2 Damaged Goods, Quarantine and Returns
text:
1. Quarantine damaged goods immediately.
Move any damaged, leaking or suspected non-conforming stock to the quarantine area in Zone F on the same day you identify it. Do not leave damaged pallets in bulk storage, picking or dispatch staging.
Zone F holds the value-added services area and contains the quarantine area. All goods awaiting disposition under PR-09 Damaged-goods handling must remain there until a decision is recorded in the WMS.

2. Apply PR-09 Damaged-goods handling for every incident.
Tag the stock, photograph the damage, retain labels and log the quantity, location and reason in the WMS. Keep the physical stock in the quarantine area in Zone F while awaiting approval.
Do not rework, restock or scrap any item until the approver has signed the disposition. Hold the affected stock physically segregated and clearly marked.

3. Observe write-off approval thresholds.
The shift supervisor approves damaged-goods write-offs up to 750 EUR. Submit the request with photos, counts and value calculation for shift supervisor review and do not split a single damage event into smaller amounts to avoid the threshold.
Damaged-goods write-offs above 750 EUR need warehouse-manager approval. For damaged-goods write-offs above 750 EUR the shift supervisor must endorse the request and forward it to the warehouse manager for final decision. The warehouse manager approves damaged-goods write-offs above 750 EUR.

4. Receive and inspect returns under PR-07 Returns handling.
Returns are accepted within 14 days of delivery. Reject returns outside this window unless the shift supervisor instructs otherwise.
Returns are inspected in Zone F. Returns staff inspect returns in Zone F and propose restock, rework or scrap. Complete all inspection activity inside Zone F.

5. Follow inspection then disposition order.
Returns are inspected BEFORE any restock, rework or scrap decision. Complete the inspection fully before you record a disposition.
Verify the return against delivery documentation and the 14-day window, open and count, examine condition, photograph damage and retain labels, then propose restock, rework or scrap. Record the inspection outcome in the WMS while the goods are still in Zone F and before moving them.

6. Obtain approval before moving inspected returns.
The shift supervisor approves the final disposition of inspected returns. Do not move goods to bulk storage, picking, or the value-added services area for rework until the shift supervisor has approved and the WMS entry is posted.
Hold scrap stock in the quarantine area in Zone F until approved for disposal. Route approved rework goods to the designated work area in Zone F only as directed.

chapter_title: Chapter 4 - Incidents, Damage and Emergency Response
title: 4.3 Evacuation, Alarms and Drills
text:
1. Obey PR-14 Emergency evacuation immediately when the alarm sounds.
Leave work, secure equipment only if safe to do so, and exit by the nearest safe route.

2. Clear all areas of the warehouse floor, which covers 6,000 m2, including Zone D, the dispatch zone with outbound staging in front of docks 5-8.
The building has 8 dock doors; do not use dock levellers or attempt to move trailers during evacuation.
Close doors and leave them unlocked.
Report to the assembly point.

3. The shift supervisor runs one shift: floor staff and incident response.
During PR-14 Emergency evacuation the shift supervisor will:
 a) sweep the floor and direct evacuation;
 b) account for staff, visitors and drivers present on the shift;
 c) liaise with emergency services and control re-entry.
Follow the shift supervisor’s instructions at all times.

4. The warehouse manager is accountable for the whole site: operations, safety and final sign-offs.
The warehouse manager will review drill and evacuation reports, authorise corrective actions, and close out findings from PR-14 Emergency evacuation.

5. Conduct roll call at the assembly point before anyone re-enters the building as required by PR-14 Emergency evacuation.
 a) Managers and the shift supervisor will call names against the shift roster and visitor log.
 b) Report missing persons to the shift supervisor immediately; do not re-enter to search.
 c) Remain at the assembly point until the shift supervisor confirms that roll call is complete and the building is declared safe.
Roll call at the assembly point happens BEFORE anyone re-enters the building.

6. Perform an evacuation drill every quarter.
 a) Test PR-14 Emergency evacuation under shift conditions, including evacuation from Zone D and all dock areas.
 b) Record attendance, evacuation time and deficiencies.
 c) The shift supervisor will debrief staff and log actions for the warehouse manager’s review.

7. Do not collect personal belongings, use lifts, or re-enter to recover equipment once evacuation has started.
Wait for the all-clear from the shift supervisor before resuming work and returning to Zone D or any other zone.

title: 1.1 Warehouse Manager - Site Accountability and Final Sign-offs
text:
1.1 Warehouse Manager - Site Accountability and Final Sign-offs

1. The warehouse manager is accountable for the whole site: operations, safety and final sign-offs.
2. The scope of accountability covers the warehouse floor of 6,000 m2, the high-bay racking providing 2,400 pallet positions and the building with 8 dock doors.
3. Site operations run over two shifts, and the warehouse manager retains overall accountability for both:
   a. Shift 1 runs 06:00-14:00, Monday to Friday.
   b. Shift 2 runs 14:00-22:00, Monday to Friday.
4. The warehouse manager holds exclusive sign-off authorities that cannot be delegated:
   a. Only the warehouse manager may sign off stocktake results under PR-08 Stocktaking and cycle counts.
   b. Only the warehouse manager may approve overtime.
   c. Only the warehouse manager may authorise new forklift operators.
   d. The warehouse manager approves damaged-goods write-offs above 750 EUR under PR-09 Damaged-goods handling.
5. The threshold for damaged-goods escalation is fixed. Damaged-goods write-offs above 750 EUR need warehouse-manager approval, and requests above that value are forwarded for final decision by the warehouse manager.
6. The warehouse manager owns compliance with sequencing controls for safety and inventory integrity:
   a. Under PR-08 Stocktaking and cycle counts, ensure a second count happens before any stock adjustment is posted.
   b. Under PR-14 Emergency evacuation, ensure roll call at the assembly point happens before anyone re-enters the building.
7. The warehouse manager is responsible for periodic governance and documented assurance:
   a. Ensure a full wall-to-wall stocktake runs once a year and withhold release of the WMS for normal operations until sign-off is recorded.
   b. Ensure racking gets a documented safety inspection every month.
   c. Ensure an evacuation drill runs every quarter under PR-14 Emergency evacuation.
8. The warehouse manager maintains oversight of shift governance. PR-15 End-of-shift handover is applied at every change of supervisor, and the warehouse manager reviews handover records and incident outcomes to confirm that staffing, operational and safety issues are closed between Shift 1 and Shift 2.
9. The warehouse manager provides final accountability for site safety, including adherence to inventory adjustment discipline, evacuation discipline and authorisation controls for personnel and overtime.

title: 1.2 Shift Supervisor - Shift Leadership and Incident Ownership
text:
1.2 Shift Supervisor - Shift Leadership and Incident Ownership

1. The shift supervisor runs one shift: floor staff and incident response.
2. Shift coverage is 06:00-14:00, Monday to Friday for Shift 1 and 14:00-22:00, Monday to Friday for Shift 2; the supervisor on duty is accountable for all floor activity during those hours.
3. Duties of the role:
  1) Direct forklift operators, pickers, inbound operators and other floor staff across all operating areas: Zone A the receiving zone: inbound docks 1-4, unloading and goods inspection, Zone B the bulk storage zone: high-bay pallet racking, Zone C the picking zone: ground-level pick faces and flow racks, Zone D the dispatch zone: outbound staging in front of docks 5-8, Zone E the cold zone: chilled storage held at +2 to +6 °C, and Zone F which holds the value-added services area.
  2) Maintain discipline on PR-11 Pedestrian safety in the warehouse, PR-14 Emergency evacuation and PR-15 End-of-shift handover, and ensure briefings are completed at every handover.
  3) Enforce site PPE and MHE rules: high-visibility vests are mandatory for everyone on the warehouse floor, safety footwear class S3 is mandatory on the warehouse floor, and forklift operators must wear seat belts whenever the truck is moving.
  4) Verify operational checks on shift: cold-zone temperature is manually verified each shift; confirm readings are logged and escalate deviations immediately.
4. Incident and emergency ownership:
  1) Review every incident report without exception and close actions with documented follow-up.
  2) Lead evacuations under PR-14 Emergency evacuation, account for staff at the assembly point and apply the sequence that roll call at the assembly point happens before anyone re-enters the building.
  3) Ensure an evacuation drill runs every quarter and attendance and learnings are recorded.
5. Quality and compliance decisions:
  1) Approve the final disposition of inspected returns; returns are inspected in Zone F and the supervisor determines restock, rework or scrap.
  2) Hold all goods awaiting disposition under PR-09 Damaged-goods handling in the quarantine area in Zone F.
  3) Approve damaged-goods write-offs up to 750 EUR; damaged-goods write-offs above 750 EUR need warehouse-manager approval. For damaged-goods write-offs above 750 EUR the shift supervisor must endorse the request and forward it to the warehouse manager for final decision.
6. Site integrity:
  1) Ensure racking gets a documented safety inspection every month and defects are quarantined and reported.
  2) Coordinate with the dispatcher and warehouse manager to keep receiving, storage, picking and dispatch flows aligned across Zone A, Zone B, Zone C and Zone D.

title: 1.3 Dispatcher - Transport Booking and Dock Scheduling
text:
1. The dispatcher is accountable for outbound flow from Zone D. Zone D is the dispatch zone: outbound staging in front of docks 5-8.

2. Duties of the dispatcher are:
   1. Book transport for all outbound orders.
   2. Assign dock doors and time slots to carriers.
   3. Release outbound loads under PR-06 Outbound dispatch only when loads are complete and documented.

3. Operate the building's 8 dock doors as a single coordinated plan:
   1. Reserve dock doors 1-4 for inbound receiving.
   2. Reserve dock doors 5-8 for outbound dispatch.
   3. There are 4 outbound dock doors available for scheduling.

4. Own the dock schedule:
   1. Assign each carrier a specific door number and time slot.
   2. Balance demand across doors to maintain throughput.
   3. Communicate door assignments to the shift supervisor, forklift operators and carriers before loading.

5. Enforce staging discipline in Zone D:
   1. Stage only verified and packed pallets in outbound staging in front of docks 5-8.
   2. Do not release loads where picked items have not been scan-verified before packing in accordance with PR-04 and PR-05.

6. Apply load limits on every booking:
   1. A pallet, including its load, may weigh at most 900 kg.
   2. Our contracted curtain-side trailers carry a payload of 26000 kg and have 33 floor pallet positions.
   3. A trailer takes at most 28 full-weight pallets, being payload divided by maximum pallet weight and capped by floor positions.
   4. Our delivery van carries a payload of 1800 kg and has 6 pallet positions.
   5. The van takes at most 2 full-weight pallets; heavier orders go by trailer.

7. Plan shift capacity to the proven maximum:
   1. Each outbound door handles 4 trailer loads per shift.
   2. With 4 outbound dock doors, each taking at most 28 full-weight pallets per trailer, outbound capacity is at most 448 full-weight pallets per shift.
   3. Do not overbook beyond this limit. Split excess volume to the next shift or add trailer capacity beyond the 448 full-weight pallet per shift limit with warehouse manager agreement.

8. Execute PR-06 Outbound dispatch as follows:
   1. Confirm order completeness and packing completion before assigning a door.
   2. Assign door and time slot and record them in the system.
   3. Release the load only after loading and door checks are complete.

9. Coordinate handover at shift change:
   1. Participate in PR-15 End-of-shift handover with the outgoing and incoming shift supervisors.
   2. Hand over open bookings, door allocations, delayed trailers and van commitments.
   3. Ensure no carrier arrives without a confirmed door and time slot.

title: 2.1 Forklift Operator - MHE Operation and Load Limits
2.2 Inbound Operator - Receiving, Inspection and Put-Away
text:
1. Purpose of the role: unload, count and inspect inbound goods in Zone A in accordance with PR-01 Inbound receiving and PR-02 Put-away to storage, and transfer accepted stock to the correct storage zone without breach of weight, temperature or hazmat limits.

2. Work location and scope: operate solely in Zone A, the receiving zone covering inbound docks 1-4 for unloading and goods inspection. Dock doors 1-4 serve inbound receiving; do not receive inbound goods at any other door. Hand over released pallets only to the designated storage zones: Zone B for bulk storage in high-bay pallet racking, Zone E for chilled storage, and Zone F which holds the value-added services area.

3. Personal compliance on the warehouse floor: wear high-visibility vests at all times as mandatory for everyone on the warehouse floor, and wear safety footwear class S3 as mandatory on the warehouse floor. Remain clear of moving MHE and follow pedestrian controls when working around docks 1-4.

4. Execute PR-01 Inbound receiving in the fixed sequence. Complete the document check BEFORE unloading. Verify purchase order, carrier, quantities and delivery notes against the load while the trailer remains closed. Report discrepancies before breaking the seal or starting unloading.

5. Unload, count and inspect goods in Zone A after the document check passes. Open, count and examine condition, quantity and labelling. Reject damaged, leaking or suspected non-conforming stock from booking and segregate it for quarantine instruction. Inbound goods are inspected BEFORE they are booked into the system under PR-01. Do not pre-book unchecked pallets.

6. Use WMS control correctly. Pickers and inbound staff share 20 handheld WMS scanners. Log counts, inspection results and pallet IDs on the handheld scanner only after physical inspection is complete. Do not create system stock before inspection.

7. Observe pallet limits before release. A pallet, including its load, may weigh at most 900 kg. Check declared weight, re-weigh where required, and do not release overweight pallets for put-away. Report any overweight pallet to the supervisor for correction before PR-02 actions continue.

8. Perform PR-02 Put-away to storage only after system booking. Goods are booked into the system BEFORE put-away to storage. Print and apply system-directed labels, confirm location tasks on the scanner, and move pallets to the WMS-directed bay in Zone B or other assigned zone. Do not stage inbound stock in aisles or dispatch areas as put-away.

9. Apply PR-12 Cold-chain handling for chilled inbound. Transfer accepted chilled goods immediately to Zone E, the cold zone held at +2 to +6 °C. The cold zone must stay at or above +2 °C and at or below +6 °C. Keep cold-chain pallets closed, minimise door openings, and record handover to Zone E so temperature control is maintained.

10. Apply PR-13 Hazmat handling and spill response for hazmat receipts. Route directed hazmat to the hazmat cage inside Zone F. The hazmat cage covers 60 m2 inside Zone F and no more than 3,000 kg of hazmat may be stored in the hazmat cage at one time. Check the current cage stock on the WMS before put-away and do not exceed the limit. If leaking, odorous or damaged hazmat is found, stop work, contain the area and alert the shift supervisor; do not inspect or open damaged hazmat on the general bench.

11. Maintain inbound discipline: keep Zone A clear for inspection and unloading, return equipment and scanners to charge, and ensure all inspected goods are either booked and tasked for put-away or formally segregated before leaving the zone at shift end.

title: 2.3 Picker - Replenishment, Picking and Handover to Dispatch
text:
1. Pick customer orders in Zone C against scanner tasks. Zone C is the picking zone: ground-level pick faces and flow racks. Remain in assigned aisles and pick only against WMS-directed tasks.

2. Confirm pick faces are replenished before the picking shift starts under PR-03 Replenishment of pick faces. Do not start PR-04 Order picking if faces are incomplete, short, or flagged as not replenished; notify the shift supervisor and await replenishment.

3. Operate shared handheld WMS scanners for all picks. Pickers and inbound staff share 20 handheld WMS scanners. Collect, use, and return scanners per shift issue log. Report low battery, damage, or read failures immediately and do not substitute paper picks unless instructed via WMS exception flow.

4. Execute PR-04 Order picking strictly by scanner sequence: scan location, scan item, confirm quantity, place to tote/cart. Pick exact quantity directed. Do not advance tote if verification fails; hold tote in Zone C and follow exception prompts.

5. Ensure scan verification is completed before packing. Picked items are scan-verified before packing under PR-04 Order picking and PR-05 Packing and labelling. Do not transfer unverified totes to packing benches or to Zone D staging. Complete all required scans in Zone C prior to handover.

6. Hand over verified picks to packing in Zone D. Zone D is the dispatch zone: outbound staging in front of docks 5-8. Move completed and verified totes/pallets to designated Zone D handover lanes. Dock doors 5-8 serve outbound dispatch; do not stage outbound pallets at inbound doors.

7. Support PR-05 Packing and labelling handover: place totes in lane sequence, attach pick/order identifiers facing out, and clear exceptions from lane promptly. Ensure pallets presented for dispatch are ready for wrapping.

8. Cooperate with outbound flow under PR-06 Outbound dispatch. Dispatch uses 2 semi-automatic stretch wrappers in Zone D for final pallet wrapping prior to staging. Do not bypass wrapper queue or stage unwrapped pallets as ready for loading. Follow dispatcher door assignment and staging instructions issued from Zone D.

9. Maintain lane discipline in Zone C and Zone D: keep pick faces clear, remove empty cartons, return scanners to charge points, and keep staging lanes free for forklift movement. Report stock discrepancies, damaged stock, or mislocated pallets from the scanner as inventory errors for stock controller action.

10. Wear required PPE at all times on the warehouse floor. High-visibility vests are mandatory for everyone on the warehouse floor. Safety footwear class S3 is mandatory on the warehouse floor. Do not enter operating areas without both items correctly worn and fastened.

11. Follow shift instructions and safety rules for pedestrian and MHE interaction in picking aisles. Yield to materials handling equipment, use designated walkways, and stop work for spills, obstructions, or unsafe conditions and alert the shift supervisor.

chapter_title: Chapter 3 - Specialist Functions and Site-Wide Standards
title: 3.1 Stock Controller - Inventory Accuracy and Cycle Counts
text:
1. Own inventory accuracy for the site. The Stock Controller owns inventory accuracy: cycle counts, recounts and adjustments. Act as the single owner for stock integrity across Zone B, the bulk storage zone with high-bay pallet racking, and Zone C, the picking zone with ground-level pick faces and flow racks.

2. Control accuracy across the high-bay racking. Maintain records for the 2,400 pallet positions in Zone B and reconcile any variance between WMS and physical count. Verify that each rack bay carries at most 2,700 kg and flag any overload for immediate correction and relocation.

3. Execute PR-08 Stocktaking and cycle counts on a daily cycle. Run cycle counts every working day on a rotating zone schedule covering Zone B and Zone C. Plan counts to avoid operational conflict, assign independent counters and ensure all counts are recorded in the WMS.

4. Use WMS scanning for every count. Coordinate the pool of 20 handheld WMS scanners shared with pickers and inbound staff. Check scanners out to counters, confirm capture of location and product barcodes, and confirm return and charging at shift end. Do not post adjustments from paper notes alone.

5. Enforce the second-count rule before any adjustment. Apply a second count BEFORE any stock adjustment is posted under PR-08 Stocktaking and cycle counts. Where first and second counts differ, assign the recount to a different counter, verify the recount result personally and only then post the adjustment.

6. Manage adjustments and reporting. Post approved adjustments, retain count sheets and variance logs, and report recurring discrepancies to the shift supervisor and warehouse manager. Track root causes including mis-put-aways, picking errors and system booking errors.

7. Support the annual wall-to-wall stocktake. Prepare locations, freeze movements, brief counting teams and compile results for the full wall-to-wall stocktake that runs once a year. Present the final stocktake pack for approval. Only the warehouse manager may sign off stocktake results; do not release the system for normal operations until that sign-off is recorded.

8. Liaise with other roles to protect accuracy. Work with inbound operators, pickers and forklift operators to correct labelling and location errors found during counts. Escalate blocked locations, damaged stock, and scanner faults that prevent accurate counting.

chapter_title: Chapter 3 - Specialist Functions and Site-Wide Standards
title: 3.2 Returns and Packing Staff - Returns Inspection and Packing
text:
1. Report to the shift supervisor and operate within Zone F, which holds the value-added services area. Execute both PR-07 Returns handling and PR-05 Packing and labelling as assigned on the shift.

2. Wear high-visibility vests at all times on the warehouse floor and wear safety footwear class S3 as mandatory PPE for all inspection, quarantine and packing duties.

3. Support receipt of customer returns that arrive in Zone A through dock doors 1-4. Transfer returns to Zone F for inspection only after inbound receipt is complete. Returns are inspected in Zone F.

4. Perform the inspection sequence for PR-07 Returns handling. Returns are inspected BEFORE any restock, rework or scrap decision. Inspect returns in Zone F and propose restock, rework or scrap for each item based on condition, completeness and labelling.

5. Apply the returns acceptance rule. Returns are accepted within 14 days of delivery. Flag any return outside the 14-day window for shift supervisor decision before proposing disposition.

6. The shift supervisor approves the final disposition of inspected returns. Do not move inspected returns to bulk storage, picking or dispatch areas until WMS disposition is posted and approved.

7. Operate quarantine and value-added areas in Zone F. The quarantine area is in Zone F and holds all goods awaiting disposition under PR-09 Damaged-goods handling. Route approved rework to the designated work area in Zone F.

8. Comply with hazmat limits for the hazmat cage inside Zone F. The hazmat cage is inside Zone F and covers 60 m2. No more than 3,000 kg of hazmat may be stored in the hazmat cage at one time. The hazmat cage holds at most 3 full-weight pallets when loaded to the maximum pallet weight.

9. Perform packing, labelling and wrapping duties in Zone D under PR-05 Packing and labelling. All packing for PR-05 must be performed in Zone D. All labelling for PR-05 must be performed in Zone D. All wrapping of outbound pallets must be performed in Zone D.

10. Operate dispatch wrapping and waste equipment to standard. Dispatch uses 2 semi-automatic stretch wrappers, which are located in Zone D. Use the wrappers for all outbound pallets prior to staging. Operate the site's 1 cardboard baler for packing waste and keep the packing area clear.

11. Observe pallet weight limits for all packed and staged units. A pallet, including its load, may weigh at most 900 kg. Report any overweight pallet immediately to the shift supervisor.

12. Support stock integrity under PR-09 Damaged-goods handling. Damaged-goods write-offs above 750 EUR need warehouse-manager approval. The shift supervisor approves damaged-goods write-offs up to 750 EUR. For damaged-goods write-offs above 750 EUR the shift supervisor must endorse the request and forward it to the warehouse manager for final decision. Photograph damage, retain labels and hold affected stock in the quarantine area in Zone F pending decision.

chapter_title: Chapter 3 - Specialist Functions and Site-Wide Standards
title: 3.3 Maintenance Technician - Equipment, Racking and Dock Maintenance
text:
1. Maintain MHE, racking and dock equipment and log all repairs across the 6,000 m2 warehouse floor.

2. Own the MHE fleet serviceability and availability. Service, inspect and repair 9 electric counterbalance forklifts rated at 3.0 t, 5 reach trucks for the high bays rated at 2.0 t, 11 electric pallet jacks and 12 hand pallet jacks in accordance with PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation. Log every repair, parts replacement and safety adjustment in the maintenance register.

3. Support the daily control regime under PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation. Ensure every forklift receives a documented pre-use check each day and that the daily forklift check happens before first use each day. Withdraw from service any truck that fails brakes, steering, hydraulics, lights, horn or seat belt function and tag it until cleared.

4. Maintain speed control and warning systems to enforce site limits. Calibrate and test limiters, signage and floor markings for: 8 km/h inside the building, 12 km/h in the outdoor yard, 5 km/h in marked pedestrian zones and crossings, and 5 km/h on dock ramps and leveller approaches.

5. Own racking integrity for all pallet positions. Conduct a documented safety inspection of racking every month and retain inspection records. Verify uprights, beams, bracing, floor fixings and load notices. Enforce that each rack bay may carry at most 2,700 kg and instruct immediate offload and reporting of any overload or impact damage.

6. Maintain aisle and walkway compliance under PR-11 Pedestrian safety in the warehouse. Keep main transport aisles clear at 4.0 m wide, rack storage aisles clear at 3.0 m wide and segregated pedestrian walkways clear at 1.2 m wide. Repaint markings, repair barriers and lighting and replace damaged signage without delay.

7. Maintain dock equipment for all 8 dock doors. Service and test each of the 8 dock levellers, seals, doors, controls and interlocks. Keep leveller pits clean, clear of debris and free of hydraulic leaks to preserve safe ramp operation.

8. Maintain dispatch ancillary equipment located in Zone D and site-wide plant. Service the 2 semi-automatic stretch wrappers used for dispatch and the 1 cardboard baler on planned intervals, including guards, interlocks and emergency stops. Log all faults and corrective actions.

9. Support emergency preparedness under PR-14 Emergency evacuation. Participate in the evacuation drill that runs every quarter, assist with alarm, lighting, exit and assembly point checks, and ensure building systems are safe to operate. Observe that roll call at the assembly point happens before anyone re-enters the building.

10. Coordinate isolation and handover of defective equipment. Apply lock-out procedures, notify the shift supervisor of outages affecting operations, and provide status updates for MHE availability at shift handovers.

chapter_title: Chapter 3 - Specialist Functions and Site-Wide Standards
title: 3.4 All Roles - Hours, PPE, Authorisations and General Compliance
text:
1. Applicability
1.1 This section applies to every employee and contractor assigned to Harbourwick 3PL Ltd., irrespective of department or employment type.
1.2 Each person remains responsible for knowing the duties of their appointed role and for complying with site procedures as written.

2. Roles operating under this standard
2.1 The warehouse manager is accountable for the whole site: operations, safety and final sign-offs.
2.2 The shift supervisor runs one shift: floor staff and incident response.
2.3 The dispatcher books transport, assigns dock doors and releases outbound loads.
2.4 Inbound operators unload, count and inspect inbound goods in Zone A.
2.5 Forklift operators operate forklifts, reach trucks and pallet jacks.
2.6 Pickers pick customer orders in Zone C against scanner tasks.
2.7 Stock controllers own inventory accuracy: cycle counts, recounts and adjustments.
2.8 Returns staff inspect returns in Zone F and propose restock, rework or scrap.
2.9 The maintenance technician maintains MHE, racking and dock equipment and logs all repairs.

3. Working hours and attendance
3.1 Site operations run on two fixed shifts: Shift 1 runs 06:00-14:00, Monday to Friday, and Shift 2 runs 14:00-22:00, Monday to Friday.
3.2 Attend and remain available for the full shift as rostered; report absence or lateness to the shift supervisor before the shift starts.
3.3 Overtime requires prior approval; only the warehouse manager may approve overtime.
3.4 Participate in PR-15 End-of-shift handover when required by the shift supervisor or dispatcher.

4. PPE and pedestrian discipline
4.1 Wear a high-visibility vest at all times when on the warehouse floor; the requirement is mandatory for everyone on the warehouse floor.
4.2 Wear safety footwear class S3 on the warehouse floor; no other class is permitted.
4.3 When operating a forklift, wear the seat belt whenever the truck is moving.
4.4 Follow PR-11 Pedestrian safety in the warehouse at all marked walkways and crossings.

5. Forklift and MHE operation
5.1 Comply with PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation for all truck movements.
5.2 Complete the documented pre-use check each day; the daily forklift check happens before first use each day, and every forklift gets a documented pre-use check each day.
5.3 Observe site speed limits: 8 km/h inside the building, 12 km/h in the outdoor yard, 5 km/h in marked pedestrian zones and crossings, and 5 km/h on dock ramps and leveller approaches.
5.4 Operate only equipment for which you are trained and authorised; only the warehouse manager may authorise new forklift operators.

6. Cold-chain and hazmat awareness
6.1 Recognise Zone E as the cold zone: chilled storage held at +2 to +6 °C.
6.2 Keep the cold zone within its limits: the cold zone must stay at or above +2 °C and at or below +6 °C; cold-zone temperature is manually verified each shift.
6.3 Apply PR-12 Cold-chain handling for all entries, door discipline and alarm response in Zone E.
6.4 Recognise the hazmat cage inside Zone F and its limit: no more than 3,000 kg of hazmat may be stored in the hazmat cage at one time.
6.5 Apply PR-13 Hazmat handling and spill response for any hazmat handling, leak or spill.

7. Emergency readiness
7.1 Attend training and follow PR-14 Emergency evacuation when the alarm sounds.
7.2 Proceed to the assembly point as directed and remain there; roll call at the assembly point happens before anyone re-enters the building.

chapter_title: Chapter 1 — Inbound and Outbound Service Levels
title: 1.1 Receiving Windows and Cut-Offs
text:
1.1 Receiving Windows and Cut-Offs

Harborwick 3PL Ltd. operates receiving from its 6,000 m2 warehouse floor. The building provides 8 dock doors, each fitted with a dock leveller, and inbound receiving is confined to a defined allocation and sequence.

1. Door allocation for inbound. Zone A is the receiving zone: inbound docks 1-4, unloading and goods inspection. Dock doors 1-4 serve inbound receiving exclusively. No inbound unloading will be scheduled to other doors.
2. Receiving hours. Standard receiving windows align with staffed shifts:
   a) Shift 1 runs 06:00-14:00, Monday to Friday.
   b) Shift 2 runs 14:00-22:00, Monday to Friday.
   Arrivals outside these windows or requiring extended handling will be accepted only where overtime has been agreed in advance. Only the warehouse manager may approve overtime.
3. Scheduling ownership. The dispatcher assigns dock doors and time slots to carriers. Dispatchers book transport, assign dock doors and release outbound loads, and for inbound this includes confirming the allocated door in Zone A and the booked arrival slot before arrival.
4. Resource commitment. Inbound operators unload, count and inspect inbound goods in Zone A. Harborwick commits trained inbound operators to each booked receiving slot during the windows above.
5. Receiving sequence under PR-01 Inbound receiving. Harborwick will apply the following mandatory order for every inbound load:
   a) Document check happens before unloading.
   b) Inbound goods are inspected before they are booked into the system.
   No goods will be unloaded prior to document verification, and no system receipt will be posted prior to physical inspection and count.
6. Booking to put-away under PR-02 Put-away to storage. Goods are booked into the system before put-away to storage. Put-away from Zone A to bulk or other storage will commence only after the WMS receipt is created under PR-01.
7. Load limits applicable at receiving. A pallet, including its load, may weigh at most 900 kg. Harborwick will weigh-check and reject or rework overweight pallets at Zone A before system booking, and will notify the client of any non-conformance identified during inspection.

Commitment: Harborwick will make Zone A and dock doors 1-4 available as scheduled, staff receiving with inbound operators during Shift 1 and Shift 2, and execute PR-01 Inbound receiving and PR-02 Put-away to storage in the exact order stated above for every inbound delivery.

chapter_title: Chapter 1 — Inbound and Outbound Service Levels
title: 1.2 Dispatch Times and Load Release
text:
Harborwick 3PL Ltd. commits to dispatch operations from Zone D, the dispatch zone for outbound staging in front of docks 5-8. The building has 8 dock doors, of which dock doors 5-8 serve outbound dispatch. There are 4 outbound dock doors.

1. Order preparation starts in Zone C, the picking zone with ground-level pick faces and flow racks, where pickers pick customer orders in Zone C against scanner tasks.
2. Pick faces are replenished under PR-03 Replenishment of pick faces before the picking shift starts. PR-04 Order picking is then executed on replenished faces.
3. Picked items are scan-verified before packing under PR-04 Order picking and PR-05 Packing and labelling. No order proceeds to PR-05 Packing and labelling without scan verification.
4. Packing, labelling and wrapping for PR-05 Packing and labelling and PR-06 Outbound dispatch are completed in Zone D. Dispatch uses 2 semi-automatic stretch wrappers in Zone D for outbound pallets.
5. The dispatcher books transport, assigns dock doors and releases outbound loads. The dispatcher assigns dock doors and time slots to carriers for docks 5-8 and confirms door assignment before loading.

Shift capacity is measured per operating shift. Shift 1 runs 06:00-14:00, Monday to Friday. Shift 2 runs 14:00-22:00, Monday to Friday.

6. Each outbound door handles 4 trailer loads per shift. With 4 outbound doors, total outbound throughput is scheduled on this basis.
7. A pallet, including its load, may weigh at most 900 kg. Our contracted curtain-side trailers carry a payload of 26000 kg and have 33 floor pallet positions. A trailer takes at most 28 full-weight pallets, calculated as payload divided by maximum pallet weight and capped by floor positions.
8. Our delivery van carries a payload of 1800 kg and has 6 pallet positions. The van takes at most 2 full-weight pallets; heavier orders go by trailer.
9. Outbound capacity is at most 448 full-weight pallets per shift, calculated as doors multiplied by loads per shift multiplied by pallets per trailer. Adding trailer capacity beyond the 448 full-weight pallet per shift limit requires warehouse manager agreement.
10. Loads are released under PR-06 Outbound dispatch only after packing and verification under PR-05 Packing and labelling are complete, pallets are wrapped, and door checks are satisfied. The dispatcher is the sole role to release the vehicle for departure.

chapter_title: Chapter 1 — Inbound and Outbound Service Levels
title: 1.3 Dock Scheduling and Transport Capacity
text:
1. Harborwick 3PL Ltd. will operate a building with 8 dock doors to meet inbound and outbound service levels. Dock doors 1-4 serve inbound receiving and dock doors 5-8 serve outbound dispatch. Each of the 8 dock doors has a dock leveller.

2. The dispatcher is the single scheduling owner for all dock activity. The dispatcher books transport, assigns dock doors and releases outbound loads, and assigns dock doors and time slots to carriers. No carrier may occupy a door without a confirmed assignment from the dispatcher.

3. Inbound and outbound slots are assigned per door, per time window. The dispatcher will confirm door number, scheduled arrival window and load reference in advance. Any change to door allocation will be re-issued by the dispatcher before the vehicle moves to the dock.

4. Outbound capacity is planned on the basis of 4 outbound dock doors. Each outbound door handles 4 trailer loads per shift. Harborwick commits this throughput as the basis for booking and will sequence loads to maintain the planned turn time per door.

5. Contracted curtain-side trailers used for outbound dispatch provide a payload of 26000 kg and 33 floor pallet positions per trailer. The delivery van provides a payload of 1800 kg and 6 pallet positions. Payload and floor positions together determine the number of pallets that can be loaded.

6. Harborwick applies a maximum pallet gross weight of 900 kg including its load. On that basis, a trailer takes at most 28 full-weight pallets, being the payload divided by the maximum pallet weight and capped by the 33 floor pallet positions. The van takes at most 2 full-weight pallets on the same basis; heavier orders will be assigned to a trailer.

7. For planning purposes, outbound capacity is at most 448 full-weight pallets per shift, calculated as 4 outbound doors multiplied by 4 loads per shift multiplied by 28 full-weight pallets per trailer. This figure represents the committed maximum for full-weight pallets; lighter pallets may allow higher unit counts up to the floor position limit where weight permits.

8. All dock loading, staging and yard movements will respect site speed limits. Forklifts must not exceed 8 km/h inside the building and 12 km/h in the outdoor yard. Forklifts must slow to 5 km/h in marked pedestrian zones and crossings and must not exceed 5 km/h on dock ramps and leveller approaches.

9. Harborwick will provide dock leveller availability at each assigned door and will manage queuing to keep dock ramps clear. Vehicles will only be called forward when the door, leveller and staging area are ready for safe loading or unloading.

10. Where requested volume exceeds the committed outbound capacity per shift, Harborwick will advise at time of booking and offer the next available slot or alternative vehicle option, subject to dispatcher confirmation. Adding trailer capacity beyond the 448 full-weight pallet per shift limit requires warehouse manager agreement.

title: 2.1 Order Accuracy and Picking Service Level
text:
2.1 Order Accuracy and Picking Service Level

1. Picking operations are performed in Zone C, which is the picking zone: ground-level pick faces and flow racks. Pickers pick customer orders in Zone C against scanner tasks and no picking is performed from bulk storage locations.

2. Harbourwick commits to full scan-verified picking for every order under PR-04 Order picking. Picked items are scan-verified BEFORE packing under PR-05 Packing and labelling, and no tote or order will be released to packing without successful WMS verification. Packing and labelling under PR-05 Packing and labelling is then completed as a committed service step prior to dispatch.

3. Pick face availability is assured through PR-03 Replenishment of pick faces. Pick faces are replenished BEFORE the picking shift starts, and picking will not commence on incomplete faces. This sequencing ensures order accuracy and prevents short picks due to empty locations.

4. The facility supporting this service level comprises a warehouse floor covering 6,000 m2 with high-bay pallet racking in Zone B, which is the bulk storage zone: high-bay pallet racking, providing 2,400 pallet positions for reserve stock. Replenishment moves stock from Zone B to Zone C to maintain pick face accuracy.

5. To sustain accurate and safe picking, Harbourwick maintains compliant infrastructure and handling limits at all times. Main transport aisles are 4.0 m wide and rack storage aisles are 3.0 m wide, with segregated pedestrian walkways of 1.2 m wide maintained and kept clear. MHE and pedestrian segregation is enforced to protect picking accuracy and prevent location errors.

6. Pallet and racking limits are enforced as part of inventory integrity. Each rack bay may carry at most 2,700 kg. Free block-stacked pallets must not exceed 4.0 m in height and must not exceed 3 pallets high. A pallet, including its load, may weigh at most 900 kg, and any pallet exceeding this limit will be held for rework and not made available for picking.

7. Picking is executed with 20 handheld WMS scanners shared by pickers and inbound staff, ensuring every pick movement is system-directed and verified. Stock controllers own inventory accuracy: cycle counts, recounts and adjustments, and will investigate any scan discrepancy, location error or quantity variance identified during PR-03 or PR-04 execution.

8. Harbourwick commits to maintaining stock controller oversight of all replenishment and picking accuracy exceptions, with accurate WMS stock reflecting verified picks, replenishments and packing activity in Zone C.

title: 2.2 Stock Counts, Reconciliations and Adjustments
text:
1. Harborwick 3PL commits to maintaining inventory accuracy across the 6,000 m2 warehouse floor in accordance with PR-08 Stocktaking and cycle counts.

2. Stock controllers own inventory accuracy for the site. That ownership includes planning and executing cycle counts, directing recounts and preparing adjustments for approval.

3. The warehouse manager is accountable for the whole site, including operations, safety and final sign-offs. No stocktake outcome is considered closed without that accountability being exercised.

4. Cycle counts run every working day on a rotating zone schedule. Harborwick 3PL will resource counts so that daily coverage continues without interruption to inbound, picking or dispatch activity, and will provide the client with cycle count results and variance explanations on the next working day.

5. In addition to daily cycle counts, Harborwick 3PL will conduct a full wall-to-wall stocktake once a year. The scope covers all stock on site at the time of the count, including bulk storage, picking, value-added services and quarantine holdings.

6. All counts performed under PR-08 are subject to a mandatory recount control. A second count happens before any stock adjustment is posted. Where the first and second counts disagree, the stock controller will determine the verified quantity and record the reason for the variance.

7. Only the warehouse manager may sign off stocktake results. System adjustments arising from the annual stocktake and from daily cycle count variances will remain pending until that sign-off is recorded in the WMS.

8. The shift supervisor runs one shift, including floor staff and incident response. Any incident report linked to counting activity, stock damage discovered during counts, or system discrepancy will be reviewed by the shift supervisor on the shift of occurrence.

9. Harborwick 3PL will maintain rack integrity in support of count accuracy. Racking receives a documented safety inspection every month, with defects logged and rectified to ensure pallet positions remain available for verification.

10. Reconciliation records, recount sheets and the warehouse manager sign-off will be retained as the audit trail for PR-08 Stocktaking and cycle counts and made available to the client on request.

title: 2.3 Operating Hours and Inventory Reporting
text:
1. Harborwick 3PL Ltd. provides warehouse operations on two staffed shifts, Monday to Friday: Shift 1 runs 06:00-14:00 and Shift 2 runs 14:00-22:00. No routine picking, receiving or dispatch is scheduled outside these hours unless agreed as exceptional overtime.

2. The warehouse manager is accountable for the whole site: operations, safety and final sign-offs. This accountability includes operating hours, service levels and approval of any work outside the published shift pattern.

3. The shift supervisor runs one shift: floor staff and incident response. Each shift operates under a designated shift supervisor who remains responsible for execution, resource allocation and communication of shift outcomes.

4. Only the warehouse manager may approve overtime. Requests for extended hours, weekend working or additional shifts must be submitted for warehouse manager approval in advance, and overtime will not be rostered or invoiced without that approval.

5. Shift continuity is governed by PR-15 End-of-shift handover. Harborwick commits to complete a documented handover between Shift 1 and Shift 2 covering staffing, incidents, operational status and inventory actions, ensuring the incoming team assumes control with full visibility of the shift position.

6. Inventory accuracy reporting is delivered through PR-08 Stocktaking and cycle counts. Cycle counts run every working day on a rotating zone schedule, and results are recorded in the WMS on the day of count with discrepancies investigated before adjustment.

7. Harborwick conducts a full wall-to-wall stocktake once a year under PR-08 Stocktaking and cycle counts. The annual count is planned in advance, communicated to the client, and reconciled to the WMS with final adjustments subject to warehouse manager sign-off.

8. To support inventory accuracy, pickers and inbound staff share 20 handheld WMS scanners for receiving, put-away, picking and cycle count transactions. Scanner transactions provide the audit trail for all stock movements and count entries used in client reporting.

9. Operational assurance activities are provided on a fixed cadence and included in client reporting. Racking gets a documented safety inspection every month, with defects logged and remediated and status included in the monthly operations report.

10. An evacuation drill runs every quarter to maintain safety readiness. Drill completion and any corrective actions are recorded and available to the client on request as part of the site compliance pack.

11. Cold-zone temperature is manually verified each shift. The verification is performed against the calibrated display inside Zone E, logged by shift, and exceptions are escalated immediately; the shift log forms part of the daily operational record provided to clients holding chilled stock.

12. Harborwick issues inventory reports aligned to the operational cadence: daily WMS stock position reflecting cycle count updates, a monthly summary including monthly racking inspection status, a quarterly summary including evacuation drill status, and an annual stocktake reconciliation pack following the full wall-to-wall stocktake.

chapter_title: Chapter 3 — Damaged Goods, Returns and Temperature-Controlled Storage
title: 3.1 Damaged Goods and Quarantine Handling
text:
1. Harborwick 3PL Ltd. shall handle all damaged, leaking or suspected non-conforming stock under PR-09 Damaged-goods handling and shall move such stock to quarantine on the same day it is identified.

2. All goods awaiting disposition under PR-09 shall be held in the quarantine area in Zone F until inspection, approval and posting are complete. Zone F holds the value-added services area and is the sole quarantine location for damaged goods pending disposition.

3. The quarantine process shall be controlled as follows:
  a) The shift supervisor who runs one shift: floor staff and incident response shall be notified immediately of any damage and shall direct placement into the quarantine area in Zone F and review the related reports.
  b) The warehouse manager who is accountable for the whole site: operations, safety and final sign-offs shall retain final authority for write-offs above threshold and for overall compliance of quarantine handling.
  c) No quarantined stock shall be moved to bulk storage, picking or dispatch staging without recorded approval under PR-09.

4. Write-off approvals for damaged goods shall follow defined financial thresholds:
  a) The shift supervisor approves damaged-goods write-offs up to 750 EUR.
  b) Damaged-goods write-offs above 750 EUR need warehouse-manager approval, and the warehouse manager approves such cases. For damaged-goods write-offs above 750 EUR the shift supervisor must endorse the request and forward it to the warehouse manager for final decision.
  c) Harborwick shall not process any write-off above 750 EUR without that approval recorded in the system.

5. Where damaged goods include hazmat, Harborwick shall stage and store such stock only inside the hazmat cage in Zone F. The hazmat cage inside Zone F covers 60 m2 and shall contain no more than 3,000 kg of hazmat at one time. A pallet, including its load, may weigh at most 900 kg, therefore the hazmat cage holds at most 3 full-weight pallets. Harborwick commits to enforce this limit and to reject or re-allocate any quantity that would exceed it, reporting the condition immediately.

6. Harborwick shall maintain traceability of all quarantined stock in Zone F, including photographic evidence where required, WMS posting of inspection outcomes, and retention of labels for audit. Disposition to restock, rework or scrap shall only occur after the applicable approver under paragraph 4 has authorised it.

chapter_title: Chapter 3 — Damaged Goods, Returns and Temperature-Controlled Storage
title: 3.2 Returns Handling and Disposition
text:
Harborwick 3PL Ltd commits to manage all customer returns under PR-07 Returns handling in accordance with the service levels below.

1. Returns acceptance window. Harborwick will accept returns within 14 days of delivery. Requests received after this period will be declined unless otherwise agreed in writing with the client. The acceptance date is determined by receipt at the warehouse, not by carrier booking.

2. Inspection location and facility. All returns are inspected in Zone F. Zone F holds the value-added services area and provides dedicated inspection benches, segregated handling space and system access for returns processing. The quarantine area is in Zone F, enabling immediate segregation of any return requiring further assessment without transfer to storage or dispatch areas.

3. Roles and responsibilities. Returns staff inspect returns in Zone F and propose restock, rework or scrap for each item. Proposals are based on condition, packaging integrity, labelling and compliance with client instructions. The shift supervisor runs one shift: floor staff and incident response, and retains authority for returns decisions during that shift.

4. Inspection before disposition. Returns are inspected BEFORE any restock, rework or scrap decision. No return will be returned to stock, routed for rework or designated for disposal until inspection is fully completed and recorded. This sequence ensures disposition reflects verified condition rather than assumed status.

5. Disposition approval. The shift supervisor approves the final disposition of inspected returns. Harborwick will not action any restock, rework or scrap movement until this approval is recorded in the warehouse management system. Approved restock items are made available for sale, rework items are transferred to the designated work area, and scrap items are moved to quarantine pending disposal in line with client authorisation.

6. System accuracy and traceability. Every return receipt and inspection outcome is recorded against the original delivery and order reference. Disposition decisions, approver identity and timestamp are retained for audit. Clients receive confirmation of accepted returns, inspection results and final disposition within one working day of approval.

7. Non-conforming returns. Damaged, soiled, incomplete or suspected counterfeit returns identified during inspection will be held in the quarantine area in Zone F pending client instruction. Such items will not be restocked and will remain segregated until a revised disposition is approved by the shift supervisor.

chapter_title: Chapter 3 — Damaged Goods, Returns and Temperature-Controlled Storage
title: 3.3 Temperature-Controlled Storage SLA
text:
1. Harborwick 3PL Ltd commits to provide chilled storage in Zone E as the designated cold zone. Zone E is the cold zone for chilled storage and is held at +2 to +6 °C.

2. We guarantee that the cold zone will be maintained within the contracted temperature range at all times while goods are in storage. The cold zone must stay at or above +2 °C and at or below +6 °C, in accordance with product requirements for chilled goods held in Zone E.

3. Temperature control is provided continuously during all operating hours. Chilled goods are stored only in Zone E and are not co-mingled with ambient storage, and all handling into and out of Zone E is performed under PR-12 Cold-chain handling.

4. Manual verification of cold-zone temperature is performed each shift as a contracted service level. A trained operative records the calibrated reading for Zone E on the temperature log at least once per shift, and any out-of-range reading is escalated immediately under PR-12 Cold-chain handling.

5. Verification coverage aligns with the warehouse operating pattern. Shift 1 runs 06:00-14:00, Monday to Friday, and Shift 2 runs 14:00-22:00, Monday to Friday, providing two manual verifications per working day. No shift will close without its cold-zone verification entry.

6. PR-12 Cold-chain handling defines the full handling rules for Zone E, including temperature monitoring, door discipline, alarm response and hold-and-release of affected stock. All client goods stored in Zone E are handled solely under PR-12 Cold-chain handling, and no deviation is permitted without written client approval.

7. Equipment reliability for the cold zone is supported by scheduled maintenance. The maintenance technician maintains MHE, racking and dock equipment and logs all repairs, including refrigeration plant, doors, seals and monitoring devices serving Zone E. All faults affecting Zone E are logged and prioritised to protect the +2 to +6 °C range.

8. Overall accountability for cold-chain performance rests with site leadership. The warehouse manager is accountable for the whole site: operations, safety and final sign-offs, and retains final sign-off for cold-chain compliance, temperature records and any service credits arising from temperature excursions in Zone E.

9. Records of temperature verification for Zone E are retained and made available to the client on request. Each record shows date, shift, time, reading and operative, and is traceable to PR-12 Cold-chain handling.
